abstracts.value: We map analytically the excitation of Schwarzschild quasinormal modes (QNMs) $C_n$ by oscillatory Gaussian perturbations across the pulse width $σ$ and carrier frequency $ν$. The excitation coefficient of each mode is determined by the product of an intrinsic excitation factor and a source-dependent overlap evaluated at the complex QNM frequency. For oscillatory Gaussian perturbations, this overlap is the coherent sum of the positive- and negative-frequency branches of the source, with its amplitude factorizing exactly into a Gaussian spectral envelope and an interference factor. We observe that the excitation amplitude peaks at $ν=ω_n^{\rm Re}$ only for narrowband sources. For sufficiently broadband pulses, the maximum lies at $ν=0$, so efficient excitation does not necessarily require matching the carrier and the mode frequency. We observe that the interference between branches, modulates the amplitude only for nonzero $ν$, a feature generic to real oscillatory sources. The prominence of the interference-induced modulation is controlled by the ratio $ω_n^{\rm Re}/ω_n^{\rm Im}$. The phase separates into a mode-only, a width-only and a $ν$-dependent term, the last generated by the same interference, with $ν=0$ being its unique maximum at fixed width. The analytical predictions are validated against time-domain numerical simulations, showing a relative median error of $\sim 4\%$ for $|C_0|$. For $|C_1|$, the median error is $\sim 16\%$ when $σ\leq 5$, increasing to $\sim 36\%$ across the full parameter space. The median phase difference for $n=0$ is $\sim0.14 \,\rm rad $ and for $n=1$, $σ\leq5$ it is $0.34\,\rm rad$. Our results demonstrate that QNM excitation cannot be understood through frequency matching alone and may provide qualitative insights into more realistic astrophysical scenarios.

titles.title: Shaping black hole resonances II: Spectroscopic landscapes and interference in black hole ringdown

abstracts.value: We apply the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) from generative machine learning to a model-independent reconstruction of electric and magnetic polarizabilities of both charged and neutral pions. abstracts.value: We construct and study a class of codimension-two conformal defects in CFTs with spontaneously broken conformal symmetry, assuming that a continuous global symmetry is also broken on the moduli space. Our construction can be viewed as an analytic continuation of the saddle point describing large charge operators and generalizes known BPS defects in supersymmetric theories, such as Gukov-Witten surface operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM and vortex loops in ABJM theory, but does not rely on supersymmetry. These defects are characterized by continuous, unbounded parameters controlling the expectation values of operators parametrizing the moduli space, and interpolate between a quantum regime and a semiclassical regime in which the local physics approaches that of the symmetry-breaking vacuum. This connection allows us to derive exact results from the effective description of the broken phase. In particular, our results for Gukov-Witten surface operators agree with localization, and we compute the $g$-function for a broad class of $1/2$-BPS vortex loops in ABJM theory. Finally, we relate the spectrum of defect operators, in a suitable scaling limit, to the spectrum of massive particles in the symmetry-breaking vacuum.

abstracts.value: HI intensity mapping is a promising probe of the large-scale structure of the Universe, but is limited by foregrounds and instrumental systematics. For the MeerKAT Large Area Synoptic Survey (MeerKLASS) L-band data, it is found that emission line stacking measurement reveals a type of systematics related to the instrument beam. Using simulations with a full-sky electromagnetic beam model, we show that the chromaticity and sidelobes of the MeerKAT beam modulate the frequency-smooth foreground emission and introduce oscillating structures that persist after foreground removal. The beam rotates with respect to the sky between two types of scans, and combining datasets with different beam orientations before foreground cleaning makes the residuals stronger. In MeerKLASS L-band data, processing these two types of scans separately significantly suppresses the oscillating residuals while preserving the stacked HI signal. The ratio of the HI signal amplitude to the systematic fluctuation amplitude increases by 81%. We find an oscillating structure in PCA mode 11 in our previous data processing, but simply removing this mode does not improve the stacked spectrum due to the signal loss. Our strategy can help mitigate spectral ripples that are induced by the beam in future MeerKAT and SKA-Mid surveys.

titles.title: Mitigating oscillatory systematics in MeerKLASS L-band H i intensity maps

abstracts.value: We investigate heavy-mass vector dark matter within the framework of the $U(1)_X$ gauge Higgs portal vector model, by jointly integrating experimental constraints from relic density measurements, direct detection searches, and indirect detection observations alongside the perturbative criterion to derive bounds on the model parameter space. Within the weakly interacting massive particle scenario, we assess the relative contributions of $s$-channel and $t/u$-channel processes to thermal dark matter annihilation. For parameter configurations lying in the $s$-channel resonance region, each fixed value of the scalar mixing angle $\sinα$ corresponds to a well-defined upper limit on the heavy dark scalar mass $m_{h_2}$. This upper limit decreases monotonically with increasing $\sinα$, with a critical threshold of $\sinα\lesssim 0.05$ beyond which perturbative constraints entirely exclude the full resonance corridor. By contrast, the non-resonant parameter regime dominated by $t/u$-channel annihilation processes is found to be excluded for $m_V \simeq 1$ TeV and above under the combined joint constraints from relic density requirements and perturbative consistency. Our results indicate that the perturbative consistency of the scalar sector, enforced via the two-loop renormalisation group equations, imposes bounds on the parameter space in the heavy mass regime that are comparable to, and in some benchmark regions more restrictive than, current experimental limits. Nevertheless, even under the application of these stringent perturbativity constraints, the model still admits a viable set of parameter points spanning a broad multi-TeV mass range.

titles.title: Multi-TeV vector dark matter in the $U(1)_X$ Higgs portal model

abstracts.value: Superconducting Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) enable broadband, quantum-limited amplification of weak microwave signals. JTWPAs are essential for the single-shot readout of superconducting qubits, broadband vacuum squeezing, or the generation of microwave cluster states. Phase-matching between signal and pump modes in such JTWPAs represents a major engineering challenge, which is typically solved by integrating resonators in a nonlinear medium in order to tailor electromagnetic dispersion relations and achieve a broadband, high-gain amplification. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a phase-matching approach using a homogeneous nonlinear medium based on Josephson elements by exploiting a magnetic field inhomogeneity. We show how the latter may lead to the sign reversal of the 3-wave mixing nonlinearity and stabilization of the parametric amplification. We envision this technique as a viable alternative to conventional phase-matching approaches.

titles.title: Field-induced phase-matching in Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers

abstracts.value: We study the reconstruction of instanton corrections to type IIB higher-derivative interactions from their low Fourier modes using modular symmetry, without invoking supersymmetry differential equations. This provides a framework for studying non-BPS interactions through their modular coefficient functions. For the $D^6R^4$ coefficient, Rankin-Selberg unfolding determines the continuous spectral overlap from the complete zero mode. Assuming the conjectured simplicity of the even cusp spectrum, we extract the cusp amplitudes from Mellin residues of the complete first mode. We combine both contributions to reconstruct all higher Fourier modes, using Hecke relations for the cusp contribution. Using the Kuznetsov trace formula and bounds on the spectral tail, we derive the $g_s^{-1/2}$ and constant terms in the weak-coupling instanton prefactor at every fixed positive charge. The leading term arises collectively from the infinite cusp sum, and both coefficients agree with the known expansion. With incomplete low-mode data, we construct modular ambiguities and give sufficient conditions for the stability of leading higher-charge coefficients. Applied to the supplied $D^8R^4$ data, these results identify the additional information needed for higher-charge predictions.

titles.title: Type IIB instanton corrections from pure modular unfolding

abstracts.value: Kinematic quantum geometry describes fast degrees of freedom (DOFs) that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and the velocities of slow DOFs. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, which depends on coordinates alone, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory governing the slow DOFs. We test its predictions in two setups: spinful particles moving in magnetic textures, and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. In the first, kinematic quantum geometry produces a velocity-dependent effective mass tensor and generates a Lorentz-like force nonlinear in velocity that can arise even in coplanar textures. In the second, it renormalizes the circuit capacitance and generates a Hall current nonlinear in the electric field. For small velocities, it reproduces recent results for electronic dynamics in external electromagnetic fields and in pseudospin textures. However, the framework can remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime, provided the kinematic states are sufficiently slowly varying.

titles.title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry

abstracts.value: High-frequency Gravitational Waves (HFGW)($f \gtrsim 1$ MHz) offer a distinctive probe of exotic physics. In the absence of dedicated detectors targeting this frequency range, indirect probes based on graviton-photon conversions in astrophysical magnetic fields become particularly relevant. In this work we show that the extended magnetic fields permeating Galaxy Clusters may act as cosmic lenses, leading to a strong enhancement of graviton-photon conversions. In this context, X- and $γ$-ray observations of the Virgo Cluster through large field-of-view instruments such as eROSITA and COMPTEL yield novel limits on the amplitude of stochastic HFGW backgrounds in the frequency range $10^{17}-10^{22}$ Hz, improving upon constraints derived from the Galactic magnetic field by one to two orders of magnitude.

titles.title: Galaxy clusters as cosmic lenses for high frequency gravitational-waves

abstracts.value: Caustics provide a universal connection between classical ray focusing and structured wave patterns. We theoretically investigate this connection in non-linear matter waves focused by a short-duration anharmonic lens acting on a Bose-Einstein condensate. A semi-classical description shows how the leading cubic aberration transforms the harmonic focal point into a fold caustic, whose local wave field is described by an Airy canonical integral. Three-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii simulations show that mean-field interactions modify the near-focus density and longitudinal momentum distribution, producing a secondary momentum-space feature absent from the non-interacting evolution. We quantify the information about the effective interaction strength carried by the $1D$ distribution using classical Fisher information and maximum-likelihood estimation. We obtain a relative uncertainty of $2.7\times10^{-3}$ for a sample of $10^5$ detected points along $z$. These results establish a framework for studying interaction-driven departures from single-particle caustic universality and promote matter-wave lenses as a sensitive probe of mean-field interactions.

titles.title: Universal Fold Caustics in Anharmonic Matter-wave Lenses

abstracts.value: Simulating a bosonic degree of freedom on qubit hardware requires discretizing its position space, and the qubit encoding of the resulting lattice determines the circuits that realize its real-time dynamics. We compare binary and unary encodings of a position lattice on superconducting (IBM) and trapped-ion (IonQ) processors. Binary encoding applies the kinetic term through the quantum Fourier transform; unary encoding uses one qubit per site, single-qubit rotations for the potential and excitation-conserving exchange gates for the kinetic term. For a single degree of freedom the unary dynamics is a free-fermion problem, and its product formula compresses exactly into a nearest-neighbor circuit of fixed size. With about two hundred two-qubit gates, these circuits resolve tunneling in a symmetric double well on both processors, with the right-well probability falling from 0.97 to 0.06 on IBM and from 0.96 to 0.12 on IonQ, whereas binary product-formula circuits with several thousand two-qubit gates do not reproduce the transfer. Noiseless emulation indicates that this contrast reflects the compilation as well as the encoding: without the fixed-size optimization, a unary product formula that captures the transfer also requires several thousand two-qubit gates. Post-selection on the single-excitation subspace removes leakage, and because every energy eigenstate of the symmetric grid populates both wells equally, the measured population reversal bounds the coherence between energy eigenstates from below. Coupled-oscillator benchmarks, where inter-register interactions prevent this exact compression, show that the preferred encoding depends on the grid size and the evolution time.

titles.title: Quantum simulation of real-time bosonic dynamics with binary and unary position encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion processors

abstracts.value: We present a systematic treatment of entanglement in two-dimensional topological quantum field theories (TQFTs). Our approach clarifies the sensitivity of entanglement measures to the cutting maps that implement Hilbert space factorization. Such maps embed the TQFT Hilbert space into a description with potentially more degrees of freedom, and for entanglement to be well defined they must be isometric, i.e., they must preserve the norms of all states. We show that the naïve cutting map based solely upon path integration subject to boundary conditions is not isometric for generic TQFTs. For any 2d TQFT, we give a prescription to construct isometric cutting maps by dressing path integration with suitable edge operators. This allows us to compute entanglement for any state, any bipartition, and any boundary condition. As a consequence, we find a non-integer "ground-state degeneracy" à la Affleck-Ludwig, despite all boundary conditions being gapped. We further show how to reconstruct the partition function of the TQFT at arbitrary genus from the multi-interval Rényi entropies of a single state. For theories with (possibly non-invertible) symmetries, we show that the entanglement entropy of the symmetric ground state can distinguish gapped phases with the same symmetry, without any further knowledge of their vacua, while the entanglement asymmetry of the vacua entropically detects symmetry breaking. We illustrate our formalism with a range of applications, from finite gauge theories to Haagerup gapped phases and infrared phases of adjoint QCD$_2$.

titles.title: More physics at the entangling surface: boundary conditions and entanglement in 2d TQFT

abstracts.value: Quantum circuits based on local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare and stabilize entangled many-body states. In frustration-free control, the target manifold is specified by local constraints, whose violations are detected by measurement and removed by feedback. We develop an exact theory of this mechanism for the preparation of Dicke states of $N_q$ qubits. Dicke states span the permutation-symmetric subspace, one per magnetization sector. Local singlet projectors define the constraints and detect departures from permutation symmetry. The resulting dynamics closes exactly on the span of the $N_q(N_q-1)/2$ singlet-pair projectors and is equivalent to a classical first-passage process: measurements move the pair endpoints, while feedback absorbs pairs on measured bonds. The closure reduces the exponentially large many-body Liouvillian to a generator of polynomial size. In one dimension we solve this process in closed form. Its slowest rate, $2[1-\cos(π/N_q)]$ in units of the measurement rate, is an exact Liouvillian eigenvalue. For any scheme of this class, the relaxation time is bounded below by the inverse fraction of pair configurations on which feedback acts; local feedback reaches $O(N_q)$ of $O(N_q^2)$ configurations, requiring a time at least linear in $N_q$. A second exact closure determines the final state reached from any initial condition. Extensions to modified transport, restricted feedback, and physical errors yield an exact transport-to-absorber crossover, geometric preparation laws, and a bound on the stationary leakage. An exact second-moment closure determines the ensemble fluctuations: the measurement noise is conserving, while feedback generates removal shot noise and pair correlations. Preparation, acceleration, robustness, and fluctuations are thus governed by one exactly solvable process: the transport and absorption of local constraint violations.

titles.title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory

abstracts.value: We present the first search for axion-like particle dark matter using SPHEREx data. We perform a conservative analysis on the first 16.5 months of SPHEREx data and derive new limits on the mass range $0.496 < m_a < 3.32\,\mathrm{eV}$ that are competitive with the literature. Our tightest limit on the coupling relative to those previously published is $g_{aγγ} < 2.10 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ at $m_a = 0.606\,\mathrm{eV}$, with a median limit of $g_{aγγ} < 4.16 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$. Cast as model-independent limits on the lifetime of the dark matter particle, the median limit is $τ> 6.5 \times 10^{25}\,\mathrm{s}$. We are also able to detect several expected emission features at high significance, such as atmospheric He I and the 3.3 $μ$m PAH feature. We calculate the Cramér-Rao bound and compare to sensitivity forecasts, finding that our limits could be improved by more than an order of magnitude with solely methodological improvements.

abstracts.value: A light scalar present during inflation generically acquires a misalignment and can later constitute the dark matter. Since it fluctuates independently of the inflaton, however, it carries isocurvature perturbations. Isocurvature and overclosure bounds together rule out the simplest version of this scenario at high inflationary scales. We show that a weak coupling to the primordial plasma can relax both bounds simultaneously. The plasma depletes the scalar abundance through thermal damping, a dissipative effect arising from the plasma's finite equilibration time, thereby relaxing the overclosure bound. If the damping grows with the oscillation amplitude, it can also drive different initial amplitudes onto a common attractor that depends only on the local radiation temperature. This synchronizes the scalar with the adiabatic clock, thus suppressing its isocurvature. The resulting isocurvature bound on the inflationary scale relaxes by exactly the factor by which damping reduces the abundance, in addition to the relaxation from the larger initial misalignment now allowed. This result holds for any damping rate quadratic in the amplitude, regardless of its temperature dependence.

titles.title: Thermal damping of spectator scalar dark matter: Relaxing the overclosure and isocurvature bounds

abstracts.value: We study the surface code under uniform coherent $Z$ rotations $\exp{(iθZ)}$ followed by perfect syndrome measurements, a setting known to exhibit strong finite-size effects that complicate the extraction of the asymptotic decoding threshold. We identify finite-size behavior of both Pauli decoding measures and the coherent information with two characteristic lengths: an algebraic ballistic-crossover scale $d_{\mathrm{ba}}\sim 1/β_R^α$ ($α=1$ for odd $d$ and $α=2$ for even $d$) and a much larger renormalization-group scale $d_\mathrm{RG}\sim \exp{(C/β^{4}_R)}$, where $β_R=-\tfrac{1}{2}\ln\tanθ$ and $d$ is the system size. As $θ$ approaches the ballistic SWAP point $π/4$, the two length scales diverge at very different rates, leaving a broad intermediate regime $d_{\mathrm{ba}}\ll d\ll d_\mathrm{RG}$ in which these quantities show substantial finite-size drift and approximate plateaus. To establish the microscopic basis of this crossover picture, we derive a leading inter-flavor quartic interaction of order $β_R^2$ in the replicated Majorana theory, which provides a route to the class-D nonlinear sigma model. The resulting marginal RG flow motivates the scaling variable $X_4=β_R^4\ln d$, in which free-fermion simulations show approximate collapse of decoding measures. These results are consistent with a Pauli-decoding threshold at $θ_c=π/4$ in the thermodynamic limit. For any even $d$, we prove that maximum-likelihood Pauli decoding maximizes entanglement fidelity over all deterministic syndrome-conditioned quantum recoveries, and that its decoding threshold attains the quantum-optimal limit, coinciding with the one defined by coherent information.

titles.title: Surface codes with coherent errors: optimal decoding and finite-size crossovers

abstracts.value: Electrical solid-state qubits are generally initialized, manipulated and read out through diffusive conductors. We show that the disorder-induced low energy modes of such a conductor --- diffusons --- impose spatially correlated dephasing on any qubits that share it, a mechanism we term diffuson-correlated dephasing. Starting from a Keldysh nonlinear sigma model for the disordered conductive region, coupled capacitively to two-level systems, we obtain the noise kernel in closed form. It decays as the inverse square of the qubit separation and changes sign with the orientation of the pair, so that qubit pairs at equal separation may be correlated or anticorrelated, an unambiguous experimental signature. In two dimensions, the correlated noise a single qubit shares with the rest of the array, in the worst-case scenario, grows logarithmically with array size rather than converging. The sufficient condition for fault tolerance under correlated noise is therefore violated, so standard threshold theorems no longer guarantee protection against this channel for large qubit arrays. As this dephasing originates from the soft-mode content of the environment rather than on any specific gate detail, we expect correlated dephasing channels of this kind wherever solid-state qubits or sensors share a gapless conductive medium.

titles.title: Long-range correlated quantum errors from diffuson-correlated dephasing

abstracts.value: Quantum error correction (QEC) decoding has traditionally been organized around fixed decoding instances: a monolithic space-time detector error model (DEM), or a predetermined temporal window, is handed to a backend decoder after enough syndrome data has arrived. This paper presents FusionQ, a fusion decoding framework that changes this paradigm by deriving local decoding tasks from the observed syndrome and then fusing their results into a single global correction. Instead of forcing every shot through the same global or windowed problem, FusionQ builds open-boundary local DEMs around fired detector clusters and expands the corresponding footprints only when a local optimum uses virtual boundary errors. FusionQ is generic in the decoder backend: the scheduler requires only a local solution and a boundary-use flag, so exact solvers, matching-style decoders on graphlike DEMs, and heuristic decoders can share the same runtime. We prove a compositional optimality theorem: with an exact minimum-weight local backend and boundary-free publication, fusing the published local decoding results yields a global most-likely error (MLE) solution of the original DEM. Our evaluation shows that, with an exact backend, FusionQ matches the monolithic MLE result on every shot. Across decoder backends, FusionQ substantially reduces decoding latency by overlapping local decoding with hardware syndrome acquisition.

titles.title: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction

abstracts.value: We apply the large $N$ matrix bootstrap technique to constrain expectation values of simple operators in heavy BPS states that are dual to classical geometries. For states dual to horizonless geometries, their explicit moduli give rise to large allowable regions in the bootstrap, while for black holes, a converging bootstrap should find islands. We explore this method in $\mathcal{N}=4$$SU(N)$ super Yang-Mills theory at large $N$, working at weak coupling and focusing on BPS states with scaling dimensions of order $N^2$. For the $1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/8$-BPS sectors, the bootstrap finds large regions, in agreement with an eigenvalue description of such states in the limit of large charges. We also present preliminary results for a BMN truncation of the $1/16$-BPS sector, which contains states dual to both horizonless geometries and black holes. Isolating the black hole states in the bootstrap remains a challenge.

abstracts.value: The Planckian time, $τ_{\rm Pl}=\hbar/(k_BT)$, is conjectured to set a lower limit on thermal relaxation times in strongly interacting quantum matter. Rigorous bounds limit both how rapidly quantum information can scramble and how soon hydrodynamics can emerge, yet the relation between the scrambling and equilibration rates remains unclear. We address this question by studying the relaxation of a charge imbalance between two subsystems of the complex Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev model and its Yukawa generalizations, which exhibit maximal scrambling. In the low-temperature conformal regime, we find through a linear response analysis that the slowest decay of this imbalance occurs at rate $Γ=2π(2Δ-d)k_BT/\hbar$, where $Δ$ is the fermion scaling dimension and $d=0,1$ is the spatial dimension. These results establish Planckian charge equilibration in maximally scrambling systems and show that maximal scrambling alone does not fix its dimensionless prefactor.

titles.title: Planckian Charge Equilibration in Fast Scramblers

abstracts.value: A central question in holography is how different boundary observables encode and reconstruct the geometry of the gravitational dual. In this work, we uncover an exact geometric correspondence between two seemingly distinct aspects of strongly coupled dynamics: the dissipative drag force experienced by a moving heavy particle(quark) and the entanglement membrane governing the propagation of quantum information. We show that both constructions retain the same underlying structure of the geometry, leading to an invertible transformation between the finite-velocity drag force and the geometric membrane tension. This correspondence reveals that nonlinear momentum loss encodes detailed information about entanglement dynamics: the leading nonlinear correction determines the butterfly velocity, while higher-order terms successively probe the local geometry of the membrane near the horizon. We further connect this hierarchy to scalar pole-skipping, establishing an all-order relation between nonlinear dissipation and near-horizon spectral data. The shared geometric structure also has implications for quantum information recovery, with the quintic drag coefficient determining the leading dependence of information velocity on initial entanglement. Conversely, the complete information-velocity curve provides a reconstruction of the reduced bulk geometry along the physical interior membrane branch, complementing the exterior reconstruction from drag. We show that stochastic momentum broadening supplies the additional radial information needed to reconstruct the complete exterior metric up to an overall scale. Our results thus reveal how dissipation, entanglement dynamics, and spectral properties provide complementary access to holographic geometry, establishing a unified framework for understanding the geometric information encoded in distinct boundary observables.

titles.title: Holographic Drag Force and the Entanglement Membrane: Geometric Reconstruction and Information Spreading

abstracts.value: We propose new candidate string theory vacua in which partial supersymmetry breaking occurs within the lower-dimensional effective theory in anti-de Sitter space, parametrically below the Kaluza--Klein scale. These vacua solve the equations of motion of massless type IIA supergravity in the smeared approximation and exhibit parametric scale separation, at both weak and strong string coupling. They are reproduced as $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric phases of a three-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ gauged supergravity. Should these vacua be solutions of string theory, they would provide explicit setups in which partial supersymmetry breaking can be studied at energies parametrically below the compactification scale. In addition, we further comment on our previously proposed solution with scale separation and extended supersymmetry.

titles.title: Scale separation and partial supersymmetry breaking

abstracts.value: Conventional helioscope searches are insensitive to the longitudinal component of the solar dark photon (DP) flux, which dominates the solar emission for DP masses $m\lesssim 1\,$eV. In this paper, we demonstrate that this limitation can be overcome: using the interface conditions that follow from Maxwell's equations in the presence of a dark photon, we show that a relativistic longitudinal DP flux impinging on a telescope mirror produces an outgoing photon flux. We apply this principle to X-ray helioscopes which employ grazing incidence mirrors. As our main result, we find that BabyIAXO would be competitive with the current world-leading constraints from XENON1T if it can keep sensitivity down to energies of $10\,$eV. Both IAXO and a proposed upgraded version would be able to reach a factor of $\sim 2.5$ and $\sim 13$ deeper than BabyIAXO, respectively, and thus probe a large fraction of unexplored parameter space for $10^{-5}\,\text{eV}\lesssim m\lesssim 0.75\,$eV.

titles.title: Long(itudinal) live the helioscope: novel bounds on solar dark photons from conversion on reflecting surfaces

abstracts.value: We study higher-curvature corrections to Starobinsky inflation, which are expected to be generated at the quantum level. When treated perturbatively in the couplings $γ$ of the higher-dimensional operators, these terms produce inverse powers of the slow-roll parameter $α$, casting doubt on the reliability of the slow-roll expansion. If instead $γ$ is kept exact, the expansion fails to reproduce the Starobinsky model smoothly as $γ\to 0$. We show that this problem is solved by resumming certain series in the ratio $α/γ$. The resulting ``improved'' slow-roll expansion is regular in the limit $γ\to 0$ and gives the same result whether one expands first in $γ$ or in $α$. We illustrate this explicitly for an $R^3$ term, obtain the power spectra, spectral indices and tensor-to-scalar ratio at next-to-leading order in the improved expansion, and show that results in the recent literature are recovered as the first-order Taylor expansion of ours. Comparing with the latest ACT, Planck and SPT data, we find that the resummed and first-order results differ appreciably only for values of $n_s$ outside the favored regions. Finally, we comment on the origin of higher-curvature operators in UV-complete theories, such as renormalizable quantum gravity, where the predictions of the Starobinsky model are stable.

titles.title: Resummations In Higher-Curvature Modifications Of Starobinsky Inflation

abstracts.value: Random matrix theory (RMT) describes the level statistics of chaotic systems one symmetry sector at a time. We propose its analogue for local quantum systems on a circle with ordinary or non-invertible symmetries. Symmetry defects define twisted Hilbert spaces, and the symmetry sectors are irreducible representations of the tube algebra, which acts within and between these spaces. Under our proposal, the symmetry fixes exact degeneracies and identifications among sectors, and ordinary RMT describes the rest, with unrelated blocks treated as statistically independent. We call this categorical RMT. For a non-invertible symmetry it goes beyond ordinary RMT, since Hilbert spaces with different twists can share a sector, and so part of their spectrum, though no invertible symmetry relates them. We confirm this in a chaotic Fibonacci anyon chain, and check the framework in chaotic $S_3$ chains. We extend categorical RMT to primary states at fixed spin in 1+1-dimensional CFTs, where modular covariance requires additional correlations. For continuous symmetries, the Sugawara construction and spectral flow isolate a neutral spectrum, which can have symplectic statistics even in a bosonic theory. In holographic CFTs, torus wormholes decorated by the SymTFT or by Chern--Simons theory realize the predicted ramp and its modular completion.

titles.title: Categorical RMT

abstracts.value: We formulate an improved scalar-fluid effective description of first-order phase transitions in relativistic theories, and test it against a microscopic calculation in a holographic model. The effective theory shows that the nature of the spinodal instability is linked to thermodynamic stability, determined by the sign of the specific heat. When the specific heat is positive, the sound modes are stable and there is a non-hydrodynamic instability. When it is negative, a sound mode becomes unstable instead. The holographic calculation confirms the validity of the effective description at long wavelengths, improving on the purely hydrodynamic description. We also identify a friction coefficient that governs the bubble wall velocity and can be extracted from a holographic correlator.

titles.title: Effective scalar-fluid description of thermal first-order phase transitions and their spinodal instabilities

abstracts.value: Galaxy clustering could strongly constrain galaxy formation models but is rarely used, because the two-point correlation function (2PCF) requires a complete galaxy catalogue at every point in parameter space. Semi-analytic models (SAMs) process each halo merger tree independently, so running a SAM on $m$ of $k$ disjoint partitions of the trees, each spanning the full box, cuts the cost by $k/m$. Because a halo's galaxies are kept or discarded together, one-halo pairs are diluted less than two-halo pairs, and the naive estimate overstates small-scale clustering by a factor $k/m$. We introduce the Sparse and Unbiased Clustering Estimator (SaUCE), which removes this bias with weights set by $m$ and $k$ alone. It has no free parameters, gives exactly unbiased pair counts, and applies to any catalogue built from a random subset of whole haloes and to any pair-count statistic. Running a SAM on 7 per cent of the P-Millennium merger trees, 68 per cent of random selections recover the full-box $ξ(r)$ at $z=0$ to within 0.05 dex in each bin from 0.03 to $30\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, at a density of $10^{-2}\,h^{3}\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-3}$: a fourteen-fold computational saving. The required fraction rises with redshift and as the number density falls, is the same for two model variants, and transfers between boxes through the galaxy and pair counts. The scatter, derived in closed form, is strongly correlated between bins, so a likelihood must use the full covariance. A recipe for choosing the fraction makes the 2PCF affordable for model calibration and simulation-based inference.

titles.title: Less is More: Unbiased Galaxy Clustering from Fewer Merger Trees

abstracts.value: The nature of dark matter (DM) remains unknown, standing as one of the most pressing questions in modern physics. We focus on indirect DM detection via gamma-ray emission from annihilating weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs). Within the $Λ$CDM cosmological framework, the hierarchical assembly of structure predicts a rich population of DM halos and subhalos. If WIMPs compose DM, annihilation inside these subhalos would generate gamma rays that could be detectable by instruments such as the Fermi-LAT. Since 2008, Fermi-LAT has cataloged several thousand of gamma-ray sources, with a third lacking clear astrophysical association. Some of these unassociated sources (unIDs) may actually be dark satellites, i.e., Galactic subhalos not massive enough to retain gas or stars and thus with no counterparts at other wavelengths. Starting from the 14-year Fermi-LAT catalog (4FGL-DR4), we conduct a systematic search for dark satellite candidates among its 2428 unIDs. We first design and apply a series of filters based on expected properties of dark satellites to reduce our sample. Through an exhaustive spectral Fermi-LAT data analysis, we find that none of the remaining unIDs shows a statistically significant preference for a DM interpretation. We place conservative constraints on the $\langleσv\rangle-m_χ$ DM parameter space, which are a factor of 2-3 above the thermal relic cross section value at the lowest WIMP masses in a conservative scenario, and rule out thermally-produced WIMPs below $\sim$50 GeV in the $b\bar{b}$ channel when assuming the sensitivity reach of the method. Our results emphasize the distinctive value of unID-based searches: they yield constraints that complement those derived from classical DM targets, such as dwarf spheroidal galaxies, and probe a unique, cosmologically motivated population of dark satellites otherwise inaccessible to observations.

titles.title: Unidentified Sources in the 4FGL-DR4 Fermi-LAT Catalog as Potential Dark Matter Satellites

abstracts.value: We present the host-galaxy catalogue for TITAN DR1, a sample of 8378 spectroscopically confirmed Type Ia supernovae (SNe~Ia) at $z \lesssim 0.15$-- the largest homogeneous low-redshift SN Ia sample assembled to date. We describe the association of each SN with its host, the compilation of redshifts, measurements of uniform far-ultraviolet to mid-infrared (FUV--MIR) photometry, and the derivation of host properties through spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting. Combining four host-association methods with manual vetting, we securely identify hosts for 7856 SNe~Ia (93.8%). We compile host-galaxy spectroscopic redshifts for 5522 objects and provide CMB-frame and peculiar-velocity-corrected redshifts. \rev{PSF-matched} photometry is measured for 7568 host galaxies, including both global fluxes and local optical-only fluxes within a fixed 1.5~kpc aperture centred on the SN; \texttt{Bagpipes} returns successful global fits for \rev{all} hosts and local fits for 7329. Stellar mass and rest-frame $g-z$ colour are robustly measured from optical data alone, whereas reliable estimates of star-formation rate, dust attenuation, and mass-weighted age require broader wavelength coverage to break age--dust degeneracies\rev{, and are reported for 5827 hosts}; in our redshift range, MIR data suffice and far-IR coverage is not required. The hosts span a representative low-redshift galaxy population, with a median stellar mass of $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)=10.22$ (\rev{60%} high-mass; $\log_{10}(M_*/M_\odot)>10$), \rev{71%} star-forming ($\log_{10}(\mathrm{sSFR}/\mathrm{yr}^{-1}) > -10.5$), and an approximately exponential $A_V$ distribution. This catalogue provides the foundation for forthcoming analyses of the luminosity step and the broader role of galaxy environment in SN~Ia standardization and cosmology.

titles.title: TITAN DR1: The Type Ia Supernova Trove from ATLAS in the Nearby Universe - Host Galaxies I: Associations, Redshifts and Derived Properties

abstracts.value: Starting from on-shell factorization and the polarization sum of an internal massive vector, we provide an off-shell continuation of the transverse and longitudinal contributions defined at arbitrary virtuality. The construction relies on on-shell constructibility and the three-point off-shell current constraint $p \cdot J = O(m)$. For amplitudes with external longitudinal vectors, we develop a method that isolates the mass-singular contributions associated with the longitudinal polarization, namely terms with power-law singularities in the massless limit. In the examples studied, these terms appear as contact contributions in individual factorization channels, and we identify the conditions under which they cancel. We give an independent understanding, based on massive on-shell amplitudes, of the polarization decomposition and diagram-by-diagram high-energy power counting underlying the Feynman-Diagram gauge and related five-component formulations. We further clarify how higher-point current constraints can emerge from on-shell constructibility and the cancellation of mass singularities. We illustrate the mechanism with explicit four-point examples and discuss the constraints imposed by a smooth massless limit. The work provides a systematic bottom-up method for building massive amplitudes free of mass-singular terms and opens a route toward a broader amplitude-based understanding of field decompositions, connecting massive and massless descriptions and on-shell states with off-shell descriptions.

titles.title: Off-shell continuation from on-shell recursion

abstracts.value: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cvetič-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-Stäckel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.

titles.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity

abstracts.value: Coarse-grained measurements provide a lower bound on entropy production, but how much microscopic irreversibility can they conceal? We construct a driven quantum system in which an imperfect counter registers a finite, strictly positive arrow of time while the microscopic entropy production is infinite. The system is a degenerate parametric oscillator below threshold, coupled to a thermal reservoir through repeated interactions with bosonic ancillas. The oscillator sustains a finite, positive heat current into the vacuum bath, where absorption is forbidden and forward and reverse trajectory laws have different supports. A photon counter with finite collection efficiency, gated time bins, and independent dark counts defines a common coarse-graining of the aligned trajectory laws. For fixed observation duration $\mathcal T$ and detector parameters, we prove that the observed relative entropy remains uniformly bounded as the bath temperature $T_b$ vanishes and is strictly positive at vacuum. The hidden contribution obeys $Σ_{\mathrm{hid}}(\mathcal T,T_b)=\mathcal T\dot Q_0/(k_BT_b)+O(1)$, where $\dot Q_0>0$ is the stationary vacuum heat current. False positives conceal the support mismatch while preserving measurable time asymmetry. Thus, finite and informative measurements of entropy production can coexist with infinite microscopic irreversibility.

titles.title: Finite Measured Entropy Production Does Not Imply Finite Microscopic Irreversibility

abstracts.value: We introduce AlphaHits, a Transformer-based approach towards hit-level foundation models for LHC physics, building on the TrackFormer and HiggsFormer architectures. AlphaHits operates directly on detector hits and demonstrates scalable full-event charged-particle reconstruction and multi-task event reconstruction and classification from low-level detector information. AlphaHits-TrackFormer reconstructs the full charged-particle content of complete TrackML events without imposing a transverse-momentum selection on the target tracks. It processes both pixel and strip hits in events containing up to $1.5\times10^5$ hits under HL-LHC-like pileup conditions and assigns hits to individual reconstructed trajectories across its kinematic range. This includes the challenging low-$p_T$ population down to approximately $150\,\mathrm{MeV}$ in TrackML samples. It achieves a TrackML score of 0.959 over all reconstructable tracks, representing, to our knowledge, the highest reported TrackML score for full-detector, inclusive charged-particle reconstruction. Building on the TrackFormer architecture, AlphaHits is pretrained on charged-particle tracking and fine-tuned for multi-task reconstruction and classification. From a shared hit-level representation, it predicts tracks, jets, jet flavour, and event-level observables. AlphaHits achieves an AUC of 0.944 for Higgs event classification, with performance comparable to a Particle Transformer (ParT) baseline using fully reconstructed inputs. It also achieves performance comparable to Delphes-based baselines for jet reconstruction, jet flavour classification, and missing transverse momentum regression. These results highlight the potential for scalable full-event tracking and multi-task learning directly from detector hits, representing a promising step towards transferable hit-level representations and general-purpose foundation models for LHC physics.

titles.title: AlphaHits: Full-Event Tracking and Reconstruction Towards a Hit-Level Foundation Model

abstracts.value: The expressivity, loss landscapes, and generalization behavior of quantum machine learning models have been studied extensively, yet mainly from a model-centric point of view. Little is known about the compatibility of particular quantum models with specific datasets. In this work, we study quantum machine learning models with a data-dependent focus by establishing a quantum-compatible form of the V-usable information. This metric quantifies the information a model can extract from a dataset, enabling a direct, data-centric comparison of different models. We employ this metric to study which data points contribute most significantly to a model's learning process. This enables us to develop an informed preselection strategy for data subsets that can significantly improve the data efficiency of the training pipeline. This work establishes the V-usable information as a powerful diagnostic tool for learning dynamics and a practical route to data-efficient quantum machine learning.

titles.title: Which data samples matter when training a quantum model?

abstracts.value: Quantum processors now measure qubits in the middle of a circuit, and the stream of outcomes is the raw output of error correction, measurement-based state preparation and monitored dynamics. For a scrambling circuit, predicting the statistics of this stream is as hard as simulating the processor, so there is no exact reference to check it against once the device outgrows classical simulation. We show that near the light cone the problem becomes exactly solvable, for any two-qubit gate. In a brickwork circuit with one polarized qubit in a maximally mixed background, measurements along the edge of the light cone form a two-state Markov chain, and measurements $d$ sites inside the edge are generated by $\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1$ qubits that move with it, while the rest of the chain, however large, acts on them as a memoryless bath. The memory of the record is therefore quantized, one bit on the edge and at most one more for every site of displacement, a bound that generic gates attain. The same causal structure determines which hardware noise the record can see, removes that sensitivity at no gate cost, and yields a tomography-free witness of dual-unitarity. On a 156-qubit superconducting processor, a demonstration with its analysis specified in advance finds the predicted memory one and two sites inside the light cone, and none where the theory forbids it. This gives dynamic circuits an exact reference at any system size, and shows that the collision models of open-system theory arise exactly inside chaotic dynamics.

titles.title: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits

abstracts.value: Quantum gravity arguments such as trans-Planckian censorship suggest that de Sitter space can only last for a time of order $H^{-1}\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H)$, corresponding to the fast-scrambling time of black hole and cosmological horizons. We ask whether this clock leaves an imprint on cosmic expansion, via a minimal modification of the Raychaudhuri equation that adds a term $-ΓH^2/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)$ to $\dot H$, with $Γ={\cal O}(1)$. The slowly varying $σ\equivΓ/\ln(M_{\rm Pl}^2/H^2)\ll 1$ is nearly constant at late times. De Sitter space is replaced by a slowly evolving vacuum (an exact Lambert-$W$ solution), and for constant $σ$ the expansion rate is found in closed form for arbitrary matter sources. The correction acts as dark energy with two components: a vacuum mode with $w=-1+2σ/3$, and a term that integrates over the history of the cosmic fluids, so that any change in the equation of state of a species leaves a permanent residual; e.g., neutrinos becoming non-relativistic shift the dark energy density by ${\cal O}(σm_ν^4)$. A covariant clock-field completion reproduces this background, and a term that rescales the gravitational constant governing cosmic expansion removes its short-wavelength instability in the dark-energy era. Big Bang nucleosynthesis constraints give a proxy bound $Γ=-3.7\pm6.1$ (68% confidence), while the negative-$Γ$ branch qualitatively follows the $w_0w_a$CDM dark energy evolution inferred from DESI DR2 at $z\gtrsim1$. The early-time tracking terms amount to a similar rescaling, for which existing fits to cosmic microwave background (CMB), baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) and supernova data translate into the proxy estimate $Γ\simeq-2.8\pm0.9$ ($σ\simeq-0.01$ today). These background-level results motivate a dedicated likelihood analysis of structure formation in this theory.

titles.title: Fast Scrambling Cosmology

abstracts.value: We study the effect of angular momentum on thermal states of the BFSS matrix theory in its gravitational and high-temperature classical regimes. We focus on ensembles with only one non-zero angular momentum. On the gravity side, the rotating ensemble is described by the singly-spinning D$0$ black hole. Beyond a critical rotation, we find that this solution becomes unstable to a non-axisymmetric quadrupolar perturbation. Following this mode non-linearly, we find a new branch of non-axisymmetric rotating black holes that is thermodynamically favoured over the axisymmetric branch in both the microcanonical and canonical ensembles. On the other hand, in the classical matrix limit, we find no evidence for such collective quadrupolar order over the matrix sizes and angular momenta studied. Instead, rotation accelerates the separation of a single D$0$-brane from the clump of branes initially prepared. The separated brane carries a large fraction of the angular momentum by orbiting the rest of the clump at a large in-plane radius. Both the angular momentum share and the orbital radius relative to the clump size increase with the matrix size. These results distinguish a collective quadrupolar deformation in the gravity limit from angular-momentum transfer to a single brane in the classical matrix limit.

titles.title: Rotational instability and quadrupolar order in BFSS matrix theory

abstracts.value: Randomized measurements offer a way to probe nonlinear properties of quantum states without reconstructing their full density matrices. For states shared between distant laboratories, we study products of three outcome probabilities measured at the same local settings and then averaged over independent local random unitaries. We determine, for an arbitrary number of parties, which third-order local-unitary invariant combinations these averages retain and which they cannot separate. The accessible information is encoded in algebraic invariants of the quantum state and is reconstructed by analysing the permutation symmetries induced by the distributed measurement protocol. Exploiting these symmetries, the reconstruction problem collapses, regardless of the number of measurement outcomes, to the symbolic inversion of a 3 x 3 matrix. As a result, nonlinear information can be extracted without inverting the exponentially large matrices that typically arise in distributed multipartite quantum systems.

titles.title: Third-Order Quantum Information from Distributed Randomized Measurements

abstracts.value: Quantum-chaotic systems share the same coarse-grained features characteristic of random matrices, such as Wigner-Dyson level-spacing statistics, yet can exhibit strikingly different eigenstate structure and many-body dynamics, including relaxation, transport, scrambling, and entanglement growth. This raises the fundamental question of whether these finer-grained features probe genuinely distinct aspects of quantum chaos or, instead, reflect different manifestations of a common underlying structure---and whether such structure provides a meaningful basis for regarding one many-body quantum system as "more chaotic" than another. Here, we address this question by introducing a quantum geometric framework that quantifies the susceptibility of many-body eigenstates to physically allowed deformations of the Hamiltonian, as constrained by spatial locality, symmetries, and conservation laws. The resulting geometric susceptibility is quantitative, providing a metric of chaos beyond traditional binary diagnostics; intrinsic, as it depends on the manifold of allowed Hamiltonian deformations rather than on the way the system is probed; and unifying, as it directly connects eigenstate structure with dynamics. For canonical models of quantum chaos, we find that minimal geometric susceptibility, maximal eigenstate randomness, broad spectral response of local operators, and the suppression of nonhydrodynamic slow structure coalesce in the same region of Hamiltonian control space. This suggests that these seemingly distinct signatures of chaos are different manifestations of a common underlying geometric structure. Our framework provides a route toward understanding the limits of relaxation and scrambling under physical constraints; in applications, it offers a means to engineer strongly chaotic regimes in programmable quantum systems with restricted controls.

titles.title: Quantum Control Geometry as a Metric of Chaos

The proofs are accessible to students who studied trigonometry and calculus. As for the set-up the knowledge of eigentheory and inner products from linear algebra is needed.

abstracts.value: We present an initial-state implementation of the Kinoshita-Lee-Nauenberg (KLN) theorem that is compatible with collinear factorisation. In this formulation, hadronic cross-sections are expressed as convolutions of parton distribution functions with partonic cross-sections obtained by summing over the number of incoming partons. By virtue of the KLN theorem, the partonic cross-sections are infrared finite by construction, without relying on dimensional regularisation as an infrared regulator. The Local Unitarity formalism provides a local realisation of this infrared finiteness, allowing partonic cross-sections to be evaluated directly in four dimensions by Monte Carlo integration. We demonstrate the framework at next-to-leading order and leading power. Using Local Unitarity, we compute the Drell-Yan and $t\bar{t}$ production cross-sections numerically; using Reverse Unitarity, we obtain the deep inelastic scattering and Drell-Yan cross-sections analytically. In all cases, a universal scheme conversion relates our results to those obtained in the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ parton model.

titles.title: The KLN theorem meets collinear factorisation: Local Unitarity for hadronic cross-sections

abstracts.value: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) needs compiler intermediate representations (IRs) that preserve error-correcting-code choices, syndrome information, and non-Clifford resource requirements through analysis, simulation, and hardware lowering. We report practical experience building FTQC, an open-source Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) dialect that makes logical qubits, syndromes, magic states, and Pauli frames typed static single assignment (SSA) values. Its error-correction-aware type system, two-level lowering design, and IR-resident resource analysis provide one inspectable pipeline to Open Quantum Assembly Language~3 (OpenQASM~3), the Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR), Stim, and IQM hardware. Case studies across three code families show that typed metadata makes code-specific decisions verifiable and retargetable: on the 20-qubit Pathfinder at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, decoding reduced logical readout error by 3.3 times. They also expose hidden architectural costs: for a three-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT-3), a magic-state factory requires five times the peak qubits of the encoded circuit. These experiences demonstrate a practical foundation for developing and evaluating fault-tolerant compiler transformations across software and hardware targets.

titles.title: A Compiler for Fault Tolerant Quantum Computing

abstracts.value: Compact object binaries formed dynamically are characterized by a tail of eccentric sources and by the potential presence of environmental perturbations. Here we show that the presence of eccentricity in a gravitational-wave (GW) signal strongly enhances the sensitivity to environmental effects, focusing in particular on line-of-sight acceleration (LSA). We demonstrate that this enhancement is recovered in Fisher-analysis forecasts and, crucially, persists in full Bayesian parameter estimation using state-of-the-art eccentric waveform models. The key insight is that the signal should be analyzed from the moment the first detectable eccentric harmonic enters the detector band, rather than from the customary entry of the $n=2$ harmonic: this allows to probe the early inspiral and thus a longer signal, over which the GW dephasing introduced by LSA becomes substantially larger. We show that with this approach constraints on LSA can increase by more than an order of magnitude between eccentricities at 20~Hz $e_{20}=0$ and $e_{20}\sim0.1$, for signals with sufficient signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR), while we predict a factor $5$ amplification even for low-SNR ones. Fully exploiting this effect necessitates the continued improvement of efficient eccentric waveform models and likelihood evaluations, enabling the efficient analysis of signals lasting thousands of seconds and containing a large number of harmonics.

titles.title: Eccentricity greatly enhances the detectability of line-of-sight acceleration in gravitational wave signals

abstracts.value: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on Rényi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for Rényi-2. Focusing on Rényi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ansätze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica. In the limit of large subsystems, these functions exhibit a striking structural simplification: locality of the dynamics together with bulk spectral dephasing reduce their functional dependence to a single fundamental frequency. Our formalism provides a setting where ETH-like statements naturally coexist for both arbitrarily small and large subsystem sizes. We discuss extensions of our results to higher Rényi entropies. Beyond clarifying the spectral foundations of entanglement dynamics, these results lay some of the groundwork for future applications of spectral filter methods to the computation of Rényi evolution in deterministic systems.

titles.title: Dynamics of Rényi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization

abstracts.value: An exceptional point of a memory-coefficient equation need not have the same signature in every quantum-state observable. We examine this relation within exact non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion (NMQSD), following the same operator closure from its coefficient dynamics to the non-Markovian master equation obtained by noise averaging. A finite homogeneous lift identifies the Jordan chains reached by the causal initialization, while state reconstruction determines which contributions survive in a specified readout. Two models expose the distinction. For common-bath qubits restricted to zero and one excitation, a noise-independent lowering-form $O$ operator gives a closed master equation. Every defective decaying mode transfers its full pole order to a suitable unconditional excitation--reference coherence. A known third-order configuration illustrates both a quadratic--exponential coherence and cancellation of its highest-order term in another quadrature. For a position-coupled oscillator in a fixed-photon-number optomechanical sector, the exact closure contains a scalar noise-history term. On the regular normalizable branch studied for bath decay rates below the oscillator frequency, two second-order coefficient blocks lead to a double pole in the conditional displacement response to the NMQSD noise history, at long preparation age and fixed lag. The purely algebraic coefficient tail cancels from the conditional Gaussian width. Complete noise averaging changes the master-equation coefficients and combines conditional width with the weighted spread of state centers. Together, the models show how causal preparation, state reconstruction, and averaging give coefficient exceptional points a precise, readout-dependent meaning.

titles.title: Exceptional points in non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion: From coefficient dynamics to state signatures

abstracts.value: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can reduce the number of data qubits required per logical qubit, but their checks require long-range interactions on a planar device. We develop a singlet fabric for bivariate-bicycle codes on a silicon node network. Spin singlets are generated on shuttling lanes and distributed between nodes, where local operations consume them to measure non-local stabilizers. We construct two syndrome-extraction circuits, based on distributed GHZ states and ancilla teleportation, and evaluate them using hardware-constrained schedules and circuit-level memory simulations. We compare these circuits with CAbLECAR, which transports a mobile ancilla between the data qubits of each check. Teleportation can outperform CAbLECAR on its original layout when transport includes spin flips as well as dephasing. Placing the mobile ancilla on our node lattice, however, shortens the mean scheduled route for the [[144,12,12]] Gross code from 350 to 153 $μ$m and lowers its logical error rate up to 50-fold in the sampled bit-flip regime. Direct transport then achieves a lower logical error rate than either singlet circuit at every sampled Gross-code point. With frequent transport bit flips, the GHZ circuit overtakes direct transport once two-qubit gate and readout errors fall below about $4$-$5\times10^{-4}$, roughly half the value assumed here. Fixing the ancilla's data-visit order reveals a trade-off between shorter routes and the correlated errors produced by ancilla faults. Source heralding improves both singlet circuits, whereas phase purification helps the GHZ circuit only above a noise-dependent crossover and worsens teleportation throughout. These results show that the physical layout and interaction order can be as consequential as the choice of extraction circuit, and that cleaner entangled resources do not necessarily produce a more reliable logical memory.

titles.title: Syndrome extraction for quantum LDPC codes in silicon: Distributed entanglement and mobile ancillas

abstracts.value: In GR with bulk viscosity and in unimodular gravity with energy diffusion, the matter sector is non-adiabatic, and their balance, entropy, and temperature equations match if $Π\leftrightarrow \dot{Q}/3H$. Disagreement over whether unimodular cosmology is adiabatic comes from assigning entropy to matter only or to the total effective fluid. The key is the temperature $T_D$ of the sector absorbing the diffused energy: comoving entropy production is $\dot{Q}(1/T_D-1/T_m)$, yielding earlier limits for $T_D \rightarrow \infty$ and $T_D \rightarrow T_m$. For finite $T_D$, diffusion acts like heat exchange with an external reservoir: unlike viscosity, which only heats a closed fluid, diffusion into a colder bath can cool an open one, breaking the viscosity-diffusion correspondence for observables and stability. Cosmographically, $Π$ is fixed by the deceleration $q$, while diffusion is fixed by the jerk $j$; thus $Λ$CDM is the adiabatic limit of unimodular cosmology but remains dissipative when modeled via viscosity. The diffusive analogue of $|Π|/ρ$ is the shift $c_s^2-ω$ in effective sound speed, set by perturbative stability rather than acceleration. If dark matter is a gas with conserved rest mass, consistent diffusion removes only thermal energy, forbids phantom behavior, and bounds the growth of the cosmological term by the finite thermal reservoir; producing a logotropic dark fluid with conserved particle number would require relativistic dark matter at $z\simeq12$. With the Hayward-Kodama apparent-horizon temperature, the generalized second law in unimodular gravity follows from the local one, whereas for bulk viscosity it must be imposed separately.

titles.title: Viscosity heats, diffusion drains: Open-system thermodynamics in unimodular cosmology

abstracts.value: We introduce a finite-memory repeat-until-success (RUS) framework for implementing rational spectral filters on a quantum computer, extending spectral filtering beyond the polynomial transformations implemented by quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). Our approach interleaves queries to a block encoding of a Hermitian operator $X$, whose spectrum lies in $[-1,1]$, and mid-circuit measurements that either accept, reject, or continue the computation without resetting the quantum state. Although the protocol may run for arbitrarily many rounds, its terminal statistics are determined by a finite-dimensional Lyapunov equation. Under uniform termination and phase-inversion symmetry, we characterize exactly the spectral filters $R(X)$ realizable upon acceptance: $R$ can be any real rational function with no poles on $[-1,1]$ and values in $[0,1]$. We provide a constructive compiler for any admissible $R$, with bounds on memory and expected query cost, and characterize the accepted quantum operation through a spectral coherence kernel. Applications to regularized resolvents and Lorentzian spectroscopy yield exact low-degree realizations and query-cost advantages over the fixed-depth QSVT polynomial-postselection baseline considered here, with all repetitions and independent restarts after rejection included in the cost.

titles.title: Rational quantum spectral filtering by repeat-until-success protocol

abstracts.value: Although belief propagation (BP) is a widely adopted decoder for classical low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, its accuracy is limited in the quantum setting. We introduce \PriorTilt, a variant of BP obtained by selectively perturbing a small fraction of its prior log-likelihood ratios using offsets determined by recent posterior and outgoing-message statistics, while preserving the same message-passing rules. We compare \PriorTilt with Relay-BP and beam search decoders for circuit-level decoding of three benchmark codes. \PriorTilt achieves a lower logical error rate (LER) than both baselines at every tested data point. For the $[[144,12,12]]$ Gross code BB144 at noise rate $p=10^{-3}$, the LER reductions reach $4.3\times$ relative to Relay-BP and $3.1\times$ relative to the beam search decoder. At $p=10^{-3}$, \PriorTilt has lower mean decoding times than Relay-BP on all three codes and achieves mean decoding speedups of approximately $2.6\times$--$3.0\times$ over the beam search decoder. For BB144 at $p=10^{-3}$, \PriorTilt achieves an LER approximately $610\times$ lower than the standard min-sum BP decoder with the same iteration budget, while perturbing fewer than $0.5\%$ of its priors per round on average.

titles.title: PriorTilt: Decoding quantum LDPC codes with sparse perturbations of belief propagation priors

abstracts.value: The compact radio source at the centre of the Milky Way, Sagittarius A*, exhibits temporal broadband brightness variability. The observed timescales of such fluctuations, ranging from minutes to hours on horizon scales, arise from the complex interplay of gravitation, plasma, and light propagation processes in the immediate vicinity of the supermassive black hole. Kinetic and fluid simulations associate this variability with turbulence and the formation of magnetised, localised plasma structures. Focusing on a single fluctuating compact emission region, a 'hot spot', we study how intrinsic source fluctuations map onto different regions of the observer's screen. Our aim is to identify distinct imprints of light propagation effects, which encode information both about the source and the underlying space-time geometry. We simulate image time series by propagating the emitted light to a distant observer's sky plane in Minkowski, Schwarzschild, and Kerr space-times. We then compute the corresponding observed light curves and power spectra, both for the full observed images and for selected angular sectors of the observer's sky plane. We derive a semi-analytical model for the power spectrum of a fluctuating hot spot in flat space-time, reproducing all qualitative features of curved-space-time spectra at moderate inclinations. Moreover, we describe how such power spectra are affected by space-time geometry, inclination, and source velocity, and show that orthogonal two-sector angular decompositions of the sky plane provide information on system orientation and lensing effects. The physical effects highlighted in this paper are expected to be present in the timing signature of accretion-flow variability, as observed by current instruments and future photometric and interferometric facilities. Further work is needed to investigate if our conclusions hold for realistic disc configurations.

titles.title: Accretion variability as a probe of black holes and their environments: Light curve signatures of a single hot spot

abstracts.value: We investigate the intensity polarization properties of the indirect images of a geometrically and optically thin accretion disk around fully self-consistent models of Kerr black holes with synchronized scalar hair. The presence of a massive, self-gravitating scalar field can dramatically alter the lensing properties of the spacetime, resulting in morphologically complex indirect images. We show that for a representative high scalar charge model, this results in the presence of high order central ring-like images at low observer inclinations. These images are not exponentially demagnified, and their polarized intensity, relative to the direct images, is significant. We therefore conclude that the observational signature of strongly scalarized Kerr black holes may not be dominated solely by the $n=1$ image, as images with $n\geq2$ may also contribute significantly to the observed polarized emission, depending on the radial emissivity profile of the disk and the observer inclination.

titles.title: Polarized Equatorial Emission around Kerr Black Holes with Synchronized Scalar Hair. II. Indirect images

abstracts.value: Dark matter over-densities around massive black holes, known as dark matter spikes, can dephase gravitational waves emitted by intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (IMRIs/EMRIs), offering a promising way to indirectly detect dark matter. This detection channel, however, requires the spike to survive over cosmological time-scales. We investigate the impact that a host black hole's merger history has on its dark-matter spike. We focus on how the inspiral of a massive-black-hole (MBH) binary modifies and disrupts these spikes within the central $\sim 100$ Schwarzschild radii of the black hole. We find that a single merger with mass ratio $q = 0.03$ is capable of reducing a spike's density by around 3 (5) orders of magnitude at 100 (5) Schwarzschild radii across all polar angles relative to the binary's plane, independent of the primary MBH's mass, with larger mass ratios inducing even stronger depletion. In fact, a single past merger with mass ratio as small as $q = 0.005$ reduces central densities by 2--3 orders of magnitude, making gravitational-wave dephasing difficult to detect. We relate these results to the MBH merger history by analysing cosmological simulation data from Horizon-AGN. We find that mergers become increasingly common as the MBH mass increases, with mergers of mass ratio q > 0.03 having occurred in 50% of MBHs of mass $3\times10^7M_\odot$ and 95% of mass $10^8M_\odot$ at z=0. These fractions are reached at even lighter masses ($2\times10^7M_\odot$ and $5\times10^7M_\odot$, respectively) at z=3. We find that accretion-induced adiabatic MBH growth is unable to cause appreciable spike re-growth between such mergers in {\tt Horizon-AGN}. Thus, in combination with previous studies of EMRI-induced depletion, this work constrains the mass range over which massive black holes can host detectable DM spikes to $10^6M_\odot$--$5 \times 10^7M_\odot$ for $z \leq 3$.

titles.title: Depletion of Dark Matter Spikes by Massive Black Hole Mergers

abstracts.value: Recent evidence for high-energy neutrino emission from NGC 1068 and other nearby Seyfert galaxies suggests that active galactic nuclei (AGNs) may constitute a class of astrophysical neutrino sources. Using a physically motivated neutrino emission model based on stochastic particle acceleration in magnetized AGN coronae, we investigate the detection prospects of X-ray-bright Seyfert galaxies with a detector network comprising IceCube, Baikal-GVD, KM3NeT/ARCA, and P-ONE. We find that the Circinus Galaxy is the most promising point-source target in the Southern sky and will be detected at the 5$σ$ level by 2038 at the latest, provided that the Seyfert population accounts for the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux up to 100 TeV and Circinus is at least as efficient a neutrino emitter as the average source in the population. Individual detections of other nearby Seyferts are expected to remain challenging, making stacking searches informed by X-ray observations the most promising approach for discovering them within the next decade. Our results demonstrate that joint analyses across multiple neutrino telescopes, together with future MeV gamma-ray observations, will be essential for establishing Seyfert galaxies as astrophysical neutrino sources and provide a means for testing the coronal origin of their neutrino emission.

titles.title: Detectability of Seyfert galaxies in point-source and stacking searches with a global network of neutrino telescopes

abstracts.value: TDE 2025abcr is a tidal disruption event (TDE) located approximately 9 kpc in projection from its host galaxy nucleus. Our spectroscopic follow-up with the Very Large Telescope (VLT) reveals C IV $λ\lambda5801, 5812$ emission, representing the first identification of this C IV doublet in a TDE. These transitions are uncommon in active galactic nuclei (AGN) spectra but have been observed in supernova flash spectra and Wolf-Rayet (WR) stars. We propose that the doublet arises from the combined effects of continuum fluorescence and photon trapping in the 312 Å transition, analogous to the mechanism operating in nitrogen-sequence Wolf-Rayet (WN) winds. This mechanism requires intense extreme-ultraviolet (EUV) illumination and a high optical depth, providing a distinctive diagnostic of the physical conditions in optically thick TDE outflows. These requirements, together with the relatively narrow widths of the broad emission lines, the presence of Bowen fluorescence features, and the small inferred blackbody radius, favor a compact and dense envelope in TDE 2025abcr. The optical C IV doublet may have been overlooked in previous observational and theoretical studies of TDEs, motivating more detailed radiative-transfer calculations for optically thick outflows. With future TDE samples from Rubin/LSST and WFST, a larger C IV TDE sample will test if this population systematically favors a compact photosphere.

titles.title: Identification of the C IV $λλ$5801, 5812 Emission in the Off-Nuclear TDE 2025abcr
