abstracts.value: We establish a microscopic foundation for macroscopic quantum electrodynamics in active media. Starting from a driven three-level system, we derive an effective two-level description with nonequilibrium stationary populations and employ a quantum central limit approach to obtain collective Langevin dynamics. This construction yields the electromagnetic susceptibility and quantum noise-current correlations from the same microscopic stationary state, providing a direct connection to the reservoir operators of conventional macroscopic quantum electrodynamics. We show that the optical response is governed by the population difference, whereas the noise correlations depend separately on the populations of the two levels. Consequently, at optical transparency, the imaginary part of the susceptibility vanishes while quantum fluctuations remain finite. We interpret the resulting noise statistics in terms of an effective reservoir occupation and a purification involving two vacuum modes, and establish a corresponding effective-temperature fluctuation--dissipation relation. Finally, we demonstrate that the residual fluctuations at transparency can induce finite heating of a nearby quantum probe.

titles.title: A Microscopic Model Underpinning Macroscopic QED in Active Media

abstracts.value: Shared entanglement can reduce the amount of classical communication needed to perform distributed computation. This can be achieved either by first measuring the entanglement and then communicating classically, or by adapting the quantum measurement to the received message. Here, we introduce tasks that adaptive protocols can solve using just three entanglement-assisted messages, while the communication cost grows without bound when the quantum receiver is not adaptive. Consequently, no bounded amount of classical communication can reproduce all correlations generated by an entanglement-assisted ternary classical channel. We establish two complementary limitations on the relation between adaptive and non-adaptive quantum protocols. First, every adaptive protocol using a finite entanglement dimension admits a non-adaptive simulation at finite communication cost. Second, every adaptive protocol sending $d$ messages can be simulated to within error $\varepsilon$ using $O(d\log(1/\varepsilon))$ non-adaptive messages. Our results reveal the fundamentally unbounded advantage of adaptivity in quantum communication, but also that observing very large advantages requires both high-dimensional entanglement and very precise observations.

titles.title: Unbounded advantage of adaptivity in entanglement-assisted communication

abstracts.value: This comment addresses the publication [Appl. Opt. 65, 7090 (2026)] which targets an alleged ``optimization'' of a patented invention conceived by the author. The invention had introduced a multi-temperature management scheme for a dual-wavelength-resonant nonlinear cavity that optimized the crystal temperature around the beam waist for phase-matching, while utilizing independently adjustable temperatures in other regions of the same crystal to simultaneously satisfy the double-resonance condition. A foundational form of this invention was initially utilized by co-author H. Vahlbruch without the author's prior knowledge during the construction of the squeezed-light laser for the Virgo gravitational wave detector. In their publication, the three authors now propose a variant that reduces the maximum achievable temperature differential. Here, I demonstrate that this approach does not constitute an optimization but, on the contrary, represents a regression that dismantles the invention. In general, a high-quality implementation of this invention fundamentally depends on maximizing the achievable temperature differential. Only then can the problematic phase differences---introduced by dielectric coatings, Gouy phase shifts, and suboptimal poling lengths at the crystal facets---be effectively compensated for, particularly in short crystals. If desired, smaller temperature differences can always be selected dynamically anyway.

abstracts.value: The nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation (NGQC) using the nonadiabatic geometric phases is a promising strategy to realize the high-fidelity quantum operation for large-scale quantum processing. However, conventional NQGC schemes combining with optimal control techniques to further improve the gate fidelity and robustness usually either comes at the cost of prolonged gate time or require complex pulse control and only are limited to several certain specific quantum gates or/and for a certain type error source. Thus, implementing universal and robust geometric gates with simple control while further suppressing gate times remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scheme for universal robust geometric gates with shortened composite pulses, where the pulse control is simple and enough available evolution parameters can be utilized to effectively reduce the sensitivity to universal systematic errors. Numerical simulations demonstrate that our universal geometric gates set exhibit much stronger error resilience than their conventional single-loop counterparts. Finally, we also verify the robustness advantage of our scheme on realistic superconducting quantum circuits with experimentally demonstrated technology. Therefore, our work paves an alternative way to achieve high-fidelity and robust geometric quantum computation against multiple errors.

titles.title: Universal robust nonadiabatic geometric quantum computation with shortened composite pulses on superconducting circuits

abstracts.value: Gravitational-wave observations have opened a new era of astronomy, with accurate modeling of binary black hole signals becoming increasingly important for source characterization and astrophysical inference as detector sensitivities improve. We present SEOBNRv5iHM, an updated quasi-circular, aligned-spin inspiral-merger-ringdown gravitational-waveform model with higher-order modes, constructed within the effective-one-body formalism and building upon SEOBNRv5HM. The improvements mainly concern the late inspiral and the merger-ringdown: we remove the non-quasi-circular corrections used in previous models and instead introduce a phenomenological intermediate region between the inspiral and the ringdown, which allows the ringdown attachment time to be chosen independently for each mode, including at the peak of the mode's amplitude. The model is calibrated and validated against 591 quasi-circular aligned-spin waveforms from the third Simulating eXtreme Spacetimes catalog. For the $(2,2)$ mode, when considering the maximum unfaithfulness against numerical relativity over a total mass range of 10-300$M_\odot$, SEOBNRv5iHM achieves a median of $4.25\times10^{-5}$, a factor of 4.5 below SEOBNRv5HM, and a factor of 3-8 below other semi-analytical models, with $84\%$ of cases below $10^{-4}$. For $M\ge150 M_\odot$, the median drops to $9.7\times10^{-6}$, comparable to the numerical-relativity surrogate NRHybSur3dq8. For polarization mismatches at inclination $π/3$, with modes up to $\ell_\mathrm{max} = 5$, the median maximum unfaithfulness is $4.2\times10^{-4}$, a factor of 2.6 below SEOBNRv5HM, 1.9 below IMRPhenomTHM, and 6-11 below the other semi-analytical models. Since spin-precessing and eccentric models are built on top of the quasi-circular, aligned-spin baseline, these improvements will make future SEOBNR models more accurate, reducing waveform systematics in upcoming analyses.

titles.title: Pushing the accuracy of the quasi-circular baseline for the SEOBNR family of models

abstracts.value: We study threshold resummation for the invariant-mass distribution of a top-quark pair and a jet at the LHC. We perform the resummation at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy in soft-collinear effective theory, with the logarithms of the jet radius treated at fixed order, and match it to the exact next-to-leading-order (NLO) cross section. We correct the one-loop soft anomalous-dimension matrices in the literature and validate the hard functions. We compare the leading-power kernel with exact real emission, and validate this comparison on Drell-Yan production. At invariant masses up to about 1 TeV with a fixed jet threshold the method does not apply. At 1-4 TeV with a jet threshold of 15% of the invariant mass, the kernel describes the exact real-emission density close to threshold but fails once the emitted energy exceeds about 100-200 GeV. We trace part of this failure to initial states absent from the kernel, which depend on $τ=M^2/S$, with $M$ the invariant mass and $\sqrt{S}$ the hadronic centre-of-mass energy. In addition, at fixed $τ$ the difference between the kernel and the exact result grows with the ratio $M/m_t$ of the invariant mass to the top-quark mass. As a consequence, the resummed correction beyond NLO, for a scale equal to the invariant mass, ranges from 1-2% to 17-23% for different treatments of this region. The upper end becomes 13-16% for a jet threshold of 20% of the invariant mass and 23-33% for 10%. The range is not a bound, and the correction is not under perturbative control. We therefore keep NLO as the central prediction. We compare the possible effect of resummation with the NLO scale uncertainty, with the known next-to-next-to-leading-order corrections, and with NLO matched to a parton shower.

titles.title: Threshold resummation for top-quark pair production in association with a jet at the LHC

abstracts.value: Atmospheric neutrinos span a broad range of energies and baselines, offering a complementary probe of leptonic CP violation. However, a JUNO-like liquid scintillator detector without a magnetic field cannot directly separate neutrino and antineutrino interactions, reducing CP violation sensitivity. This study investigates whether machine learning based statistical separation can improve CP violation sensitivity in a 20-kton detector. $ν_μ$ and $ν_e$ charged current events are generated with GENIE (using Honda flux) in a JUNO-like detector geometry and are reweighted using OscProb three flavor oscillation probabilities incorporating Earth matter effects and NuFIT parameters. Detector response is approximated by smearing lepton and hadronic energies, neutrino direction, and neutron multiplicity. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron (MLP) classifiers are trained on inelasticity, neutron multiplicity, and charged lepton energy, with XGBoost selected for the analysis. CP violation sensitivity is evaluated for a 200 kton-year exposure using a Poisson likelihood with systematic nuisance parameters and marginalization over five oscillation parameters within their respective $3σ$ ranges. XGBoost achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of approximately 0.83 for both flavor samples. Under the square root approximation, peak CP violation sensitivity improves from 1.49 $σ$ to 1.96 $σ$ for normal mass ordering and from 1.14 $σ$ to 1.61 $σ$ for inverted mass ordering. Machine learning based statistical neutrino-antineutrino separation can recover part of the CP violation sensitivity lost in charge blind detectors. These preliminary results motivate further studies incorporating validated detector response and systematic uncertainties.

titles.title: Machine learning assisted $ν/\barν$ discrimination in atmospheric neutrino events for CPV sensitivity in a 20-kton liquid scintillator detector

abstracts.value: Sklar's theorem in classical probability theory rigorously separates the marginal statistics of a joint probability distribution from its dependence structure data. We apply this perspective to the context-dependent classical probability tables induced by the Born rule for a quantum state. For each Born probability table of a given quantum state, we discard the marginal statistics of the individual parties, retaining only the relational data among them. Yet we prove that, when these classical relational data are collected over all contexts, the nontrivial quantum compatibility constraints inherent in quantum mechanics suffice to reconstruct any irreducible multiqubit quantum state itself. This means that the local information of the subsystems, discarded table by table, is fully recovered. We call this quantum-state reconstruction from Sklar-type relational data.

titles.title: Quantum State Reconstruction from Sklar-Type Relational Data

abstracts.value: Silicon quantum-dot spin qubits are among the most promising routes to large-scale quantum computation, but the residual 29Si nuclear spins in natural silicon impose a hyperfine dephasing limit that must be overcome by isotopic purification. Here, we report the epitaxial growth of high-purity 28Si on float-zone silicon using an industrial reduced-pressure chemical vapor deposition (RPCVD) system. Secondary-ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) confirms an 28Si isotopic purity of 99.997%, with the 29Si concentration below 30 ppm. Through a systematic vacuum annealing matrix (850-1150 C), combined with atomic force microscopy and SIMS, we investigate the defect-mediated decomposition of the native oxide and the injection of non-equilibrium vacancies. We identify a thermal-budget window below 950 C within which the thin-layer structure of 28Si remains intact. At 1.5 K, magnetotransport measurements reveal a peak Hall mobility of 12,858 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and a quantum scattering lifetime of 0.659 ps, corresponding to a single-particle level broadening of 499 micro-eV. A double quantum dot fabricated on this platform exhibits a T2* of 0.62 us, a Hahn-echo coherence time of 28.8 us, and single-qubit gate fidelities of up to 99.9% measured by randomized benchmarking. Our results establish industrial RPCVD as a promising route toward high-coherence, high-fidelity silicon spin qubits.

titles.title: Industrial RPCVD growth of high-purity 28Si epilayers with 29Si content below 30 ppm for high-fidelity electron spin qubits

abstracts.value: We study the connection between asymmetric dark matter and nanohertz gravitational waves from a supercooled first-order phase transition in a classically conformal dark sector. The dark sector contains a real scalar, a complex scalar and a Dirac fermion, whose mass arises from radiative symmetry breaking. An additional Affleck--Dine condensate generates a fermion asymmetry and heats the dark bath before nucleation. The conserved dark charge fixes the asymmetry between fermions and antifermions, while entropy production during delayed visible-sector reheating dilutes the relic and determines the redshift of the gravitational-wave spectrum. We calculate the thermal nucleation rate in a three-dimensional effective theory with finite-density corrections, next-to-leading-order contributions and fluctuation determinants (NLOdet). We follow the coupled thermal evolution of the dark and visible sectors. For a benchmark chosen to match the observed dark-matter abundance, the transition completes at MeV-scale temperatures and produces a nanohertz signal under the adopted dynamical and thermal assumptions. We compare the predicted collision-dominated gravitational-wave spectra with free-spectrum posteriors from pulsar timing arrays. For a benchmark point and variations of the dark-sector parameters, the gravitational-wave spectra and dark matter relic abundances are compared, and compatibility with Big Bang nucleosynthesis is assessed.

titles.title: Nanohertz gravitational waves and asymmetric dark matter from a supercooled dark sector phase transition

abstracts.value: Spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) generates correlated photon pairs that inherently exhibit high-dimensional spatial entanglement in orbital angular momentum (OAM) modes. In practice, the resulting two-photon states are typically not maximally entangled due to a highly non-uniform distribution of generated OAM modes. Although pump-beam engineering has emerged as a tool to prepare high-dimensional entangled states, it has usually been restricted to low-dimensional subspaces, i.e., small sets of selected OAM modes for each photon within the full infinite-dimensional two-photon Hilbert space. A general understanding of the requirements for the generation of maximally entangled states (MESs) for any dimensionality $d$ with $d>2$ is lacking. Here, we demonstrate how pump engineering enables the generation of high-dimensional MESs for arbitrary $d$ defined in $d \times d$ subspaces. By identifying the interplay between the spatial pump structure and the choice of OAM subspace, the required pump profile for a target MES is directly determined. Our results reveal that maximal entanglement with OAM requires a careful and nontrivial design of the effective high-dimensional Hilbert subspace.

titles.title: High-Dimensional Maximally Entangled OAM States by Joint Pump and Modal-Space Engineering

abstracts.value: Nuclear form factor measurements can be used to extract the nuclear charge radius. These can be compared to ab initio nuclear structure calculations, with the difference between 3H and 3He charge radii providing information on the spatial distribution of protons vs neutrons in these nuclei. Extractions of the 3H-3He charge radius difference are limited by the modest amount of data for tritium elastic scattering at low momentum transfer. The experiment made a precise measurement of the 3H/3He form factor ratio at low momentum transfer which is combined with the absolute 3He measurements to provide improved 3H data. This provides an improved determination of the absolute normalization corrections of world data sets, giving improved precision for the low-Q^2 measurements that are most sensitive to the radius. We extract the elastic cross sections and the 3H/3He ratio at Q^2=3.03 fm^{-2} and evaluate the impact of this point on a global fit of previous form factor extractions. We examine both the impact on the normalizations of the other data sets and the fit parameters, including the charge radius and its uncertainty. Our sensitivity study shows that the new precision data points constrain the normalization of previous data sets, reducing the uncertainties by up to 12% and yielding a 4% improvement in the radius. Including projected data based on an approved experiment yields improvements in the normalization factors of up to 20% and a 27% improvement in the 3H RMS charge radius extraction, allowing for an improved extraction of the 3H-3He radius difference from a direct fit to the form factor ratios over a range in Q^2.

titles.title: Precise measurements of the 3H/3He charge form factor ratio and their impact on the 3H-3He charge radius difference

abstracts.value: We investigate the nonlinear scalarization of Reissner-Nordström black holes in scalar-torsion-Maxwell teleparallel gravity, in which the scalar field is nonminimally coupled to the Weitzenböck invariant. We consider polynomial coupling functions that avoid tachyonic instabilities at the linear level, thereby exploring a scalarization mechanism driven by nonlinear effects. In the decoupling limit, we study the nonlinear evolution of finite-amplitude scalar perturbations and show that the inclusion of a sixth-order coupling term allows the scalar field to dynamically evolve toward nontrivial stationary configurations. This behavior can be understood in terms of the effective potential, which develops nontrivial local minima that provide a mechanism for nonlinear saturation. By numerically solving the fully coupled field equations, we construct asymptotically flat charged black hole solutions endowed with scalar hair. We classify these solutions according to the number of nodes in the scalar field profile, identifying multiple branches whose structure and multiplicity depend on the coupling parameters. We further show that the higher-order coupling progressively suppresses higher-node branches and characterize the scalar backreaction through deviations of the metric functions and the torsion scalar from the Reissner-Nordström background.

titles.title: Nonlinear Scalarization of Reissner-Nordström Black Holes in Scalar-Torsion-Maxwell Teleparallel Gravity

abstracts.value: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.

titles.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos

abstracts.value: The precision era of jet-quenching phenomenology requires a quantitative control of medium-induced gluon radiation. We consider the BDMPS-Z spectrum in the soft-gluon limit for a Yukawa (Gyulassy-Wang) potential. Writing the Yukawa dipole cross section as a Laplace superposition of Gaussians, we express the fully resummed spectrum as an average over Poisson-distributed configurations of Gaussian scattering centers, each of which is solved in closed form. This yields a master formula for the spectrum both differential in the transverse momentum $k_\perp$ and integrated with a cut on $k_\perp$, valid for static and expanding media with arbitrary profiles. Its evaluation by Monte Carlo sampling of the configurations is efficient and trivially parallelizable. The method reproduces the first order in opacity and published results without kinematic cuts, while with a cut we find sizeable relative deviations from previous results. We argue that the same construction extends to the more complex building blocks of an in-medium parton cascade, such as finite energy fraction and emissions off color antennas, and provides a natural starting point for analytical approximations. The code is publicly available.

titles.title: A Poisson-gas approach to medium-induced gluon radiation

abstracts.value: Light bosons beyond the Standard Model can mediate exotic spin-dependent interactions between electrons, motivating sensitive searches at short distances. We propose a magnetic resonance force microscopy (MRFM) scheme that exploits oscillating-cantilever-driven adiabatic reversals (OSCAR) of electron spins to convert these interactions into measurable mechanical signals. The ferromagnetic tip serves as both a dense polarized-spin source and a source of magnetic-field gradients, enabling force detection without magnetic shielding between the source and sensor. Within a linearized treatment of the coupled spin-mechanical dynamics, we derive resonance-frequency shifts associated with the $V_2$ and $V_3$ interactions and a second-harmonic force signal arising from the velocity-dependent $V_8$ interaction. We further investigate interrupted-OSCAR differential detection and distance-dependent measurements to discriminate exotic signals from conventional magnetic backgrounds. Using representative parameters from ensemble and single-spin MRFM experiments, we estimate the projected sensitivity under specified noise and statistical assumptions. The results suggest that the proposed scheme could provide complementary sensitivity to short-range spin-dependent interactions, with the potential to improve existing constraints on $V_2$ over selected submicrometer interaction ranges. Our study establishes adiabatic spin-inversion MRFM as a promising approach to probing exotic electron-electron forces.

titles.title: Probing Exotic Electron-Electron Interactions via Adiabatic Spin Inversion in MRFM

abstracts.value: We present a measurement of the baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) feature using the largest galaxy cluster sample with spectroscopic redshift information to date, comprising 169,679 clusters selected from the WH24 catalogue based on the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. We measure the two-point correlation function in two redshift bins, $0.17\leq z<0.35$ and $0.35\leq z<0.5$, corresponding to effective redshifts of $z_{\rm eff}=0.25$ and $0.43$, with the BAO feature detected at approximately the $4σ$ level or above in both bins. By fitting the measured correlation functions, we obtain dilation parameters of $α=0.97\pm0.07$ and $α=1.01\pm0.04$, corresponding to volume-averaged distance measurements of $D_V/r_d=6.70\pm0.48$ and $D_V/r_d=11.25\pm0.47$, respectively. Using the Planck 2018 sound horizon calibration, we obtain $H_0=66.6 \pm 4.9 \,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ within the flat $Λ$CDM framework. We further combine our cluster BAO measurements with cosmic microwave background and Pantheon+ Type Ia supernova observations to constrain dynamical dark energy within the Chevallier--Polarski--Linder parametrization. The resulting constraints are consistent with $Λ$CDM, which lies within the $68\%$ joint credible region in the $w_0$--$w_a$ plane. Our results demonstrate the potential of galaxy clusters as complementary tracers for BAO measurements and cosmological constraints.

titles.title: Detecting Baryon Acoustic Oscillations from Galaxy Clusters: Distance Constraints

abstracts.value: The Galactic Center is home to the largest known concentration of X-ray sources ever detected in our Galaxy, including a sizable population of accreting compact objects. Utilizing data from the XMM-Newton Galactic Plane Heritage Survey of the central $20^{\circ}\times2^{\circ}$ of the Milky Way, we investigate the varying source populations in the inner regions of the Galaxy. We identify for the first time a concentration of extremely hard X-ray sources within $|l|<1.3^{\circ}$ and $|b|<0.3^{\circ}$, a region that overlaps the nuclear stellar disk (NSD). We determine that this hardness is intrinsic to the sources and not a manifestation of high line-of-sight column density ($N_{\rm H}$). Unlike the "soft" X-ray sources, this population does not trace the stellar mass distribution, indicating an overabundance compared to the underlying stellar population. We simulate spectra for a variety of source types to model their X-ray hardness and compare their distributions to those we observed in our survey data. We find that a significant subset of the Galactic Center X-ray population may comprise intermediate polars (IPs) with massive white dwarfs, possibly formed through dynamical processes. Our study provides novel observational insights into the distribution of stellar remnants and other X-ray sources in the vicinity of our supermassive black hole, Sgr A*.

titles.title: Unveiling a Concentration of Hard X-Ray Point Sources in the Nuclear Stellar Disk with XMM-Newton

abstracts.value: The cost of Pauli propagation depends on the local basis in which the evolving operator is expanded. We show that its Pauli complexity splits into an occupation part, invariant under local rotations and bounded from below by the operator mass and length distributions, and a flavour part that a suitable basis can remove. We introduce frame-adaptive Pauli propagation (FAPP), which rotates the basis of every qubit, gate by gate, to the principal axes of the operator's local polarisation, exactly and within the memory structure of Pauli propagation. This simple rule achieves most of what the best local frame can, and the polarisation predicts how much any local frame can gain. In the Ising chain in transverse and longitudinal fields, FAPP lowers the truncation error at fixed memory by up to an order of magnitude and the memory by a size-independent factor of three; on the infinite two-dimensional lattice it needs up to seven times fewer strings for a given certified accuracy, and in Clifford circuits doped with T gates two to eight times fewer.

titles.title: Pauli propagation in adaptive local frames

abstracts.value: We present a prescription for identifying decoupled sectors of 4d SCFTs obtained from compactifications of branes. Central to our analysis is the comparison of anomaly polynomials obtained via field-theoretic reduction versus anomaly inflow. Our flagship examples are the 4d $\mathcal{N}=1$ SCFTs obtained by compactifying the 6d $(1,0)$ theory from M5-branes probing a $\mathbb{C}^2/\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold singularity on a torus with flux. The anomaly polynomial of the interacting fixed point is known to decompose into the $T^2$ reduction of the 6d anomaly polynomial, plus a contribution from flip fields introduced to remove operators from the spectrum. Adopting the inflow perspective, the contribution from the flipped sector is obtained as the difference between inflow anomaly polynomials in the singular and resolved geometries, which we efficiently compute using equivariant localization. Helpfully, the 4d SCFTs admit two dual quiver gauge theory descriptions: $Y^{p,q}$ quiver gauge theories, and class $\mathcal{S}_2$ necklace quivers obtained from trinions. We study the interacting and decoupled sectors on both sides of the duality and construct an explicit map between their chiral rings, identifying a range of parameter space for which the quivers flow to apparently different interacting fixed points. Each chiral ring generator is furthermore matched to an M2-brane wrapping a 2-cycle in the resolved M-theory geometry.

titles.title: Decoupling Across Dimensions

abstracts.value: Sequential kinetic freeze-out in high-energy collisions probes the dynamics governing the final stages of strongly interacting matter. Inspired by the recently established quadruple freeze-out scenario, we present a thermodynamic analysis of transverse momentum spectra for a set of identified particles produced in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 2.76$ and $7$ TeV. Using a modified Tsallis-Pareto function, we extract the effective temperature and the non-extensivity parameter for each species. We observe a robust five-layer hierarchy in the effective temperature. At both energies, the layers are: non-strange hadrons, singly-strange hadrons, multi-strange hadrons, light nuclei, and the $ϕ(1020)$ meson. At $7$~TeV, the $η$ meson joins the $ϕ(1020)$ meson in the highest-temperature layer. At both energies, each pair of neighboring layers is separated by more than $ 3σ$, and the separation at the top exceeds $7σ$. The grouping persists at both energies, while the temperatures shift upward at 7 TeV. The observed pattern shows that the decoupling sequence is driven by an interplay of strangeness, cross-sections, and the OZI rule rather than by particle mass alone. Notably, the $ϕ(1020)$ meson has a mass close to the proton, but a significantly higher temperature due to its OZI-suppressed coupling to the hadronic medium. The unexpected coincidence of $η$ and $ϕ(1020)$ at 7 TeV presents a puzzle that may point to a common early production mechanism or in-medium effects, which are not yet understood. The five-layer hierarchy provides new constraints on theoretical models of hadronization. It suggests that the sequential decoupling of particles from the evolving medium is even more sensitive to their internal structure and interaction than previously assumed, with implications for the QGP-like matter formation in small systems.

titles.title: The $ϕ$-$η$ Puzzle and the Five-Layer Effective-Temperature Hierarchy in $pp$ Collisions at 2.76 and 7 TeV

abstracts.value: Machine-learned circuit parameters could remove one of the main bottlenecks of variational quantum eigensolvers: the classical optimization loop, with its typical barren plateaus, local minima, and costly energy and gradient evaluations, is replaced by a direct prediction. Prior work showed that machine-learning models paired with a structured circuit design can transfer across system size and structure within hydrogenic systems. The next step: Extending them to organic molecules would seem to require re-training on use-case-specific training sets. In this work, we show that this is not necessary by establishing an alchemical approach. A geometric projection places surrogate hydrogen atoms along the bond directions of the target molecule and so maps its local bonding environment onto small hydrogenic fragments. Existing hydrogenic solvers can then be reused as they are. The only new quantity is a single projection radius per bond type, which is fitted once on a small reference molecule and reused unchanged thereafter. We demonstrate the approach on the separable-pair circuit designs that have been used in prior work and extend the approach to multi-circuit approaches that span effective bases for quantum subspaces.

titles.title: Alchemically Transferable Parameters for Variational Quantum Eigensolvers

abstracts.value: Charm production in hadronic collisions proceeds via many different processes, which makes it hard to calculate from first principles. Using PYTHIA simulations, we study correlations between charm and anticharm hadrons and show that hard-process charm, final-state splitting charm, and initial-state-shower charm populate markedly different regions of rapidity and azimuthal-angle difference. In particular, selections on the pair rapidity separation, $Δy$, can strongly enrich or suppress the near-side final-state splitting contribution and thereby provide experimental sensitivity to the different production processes. A comparison with existing LHCb $D^0\bar{D}^0$ correlation measurements from Run 1 motivates more differential studies using the substantially larger LHC data sets now available. Extending such measurements to heavy-ion collisions could further distinguish medium modifications of charm produced directly in the hard scattering from charm originating from a parent gluon, providing a new handle on the different interactions of heavy quarks and gluons with the quark-gluon plasma.

titles.title: How to isolate charm production mechanisms using charm-anticharm rapidity and azimuthal angle differences

abstracts.value: Information replication occurs when a single locally encoded classical bit becomes simultaneously readable across extensively many disjoint regions of a quantum many-body system. Here we identify dynamical selection as a mechanism for generating these records, whereby an unperturbed nonthermal reference remains locally recognizable while its locally perturbed counterpart spreads and relaxes under the same Hamiltonian. We establish an entropy-capacity criterion showing that a uniform area-law reference paired with a volume-law perturbed branch guarantees extensive records at a fixed, nonzero information threshold. An embedded-dimer chain demonstrates both record proliferation and increasing readout reliability with fragment size, while stabilized PXP dynamics extends the mechanism to a coherently recurrent reference. These results characterize information spreading through the spatial multiplicity of accessible records and provide experimental signatures measurable via fixed local readouts.

titles.title: One Bit, Many Records: Information Replication in Quantum Many-Body Dynamics

abstracts.value: Fourteen years after its discovery, the Higgs boson has changed roles. It was once the object of the search, but today it is an instrument with which we interrogate Nature's vacuum, test quantum field theory and look for new principles. This shift comes at a time when, unlike before the Higgs discovery, we have no theoretical argument guaranteeing new physics within experimental reach. At the same time, securing long-term support for fundamental science is becoming increasingly challenging. I revisit the path from a theoretically motivated discovery to a precision programme, explain why the Higgs is such an unusual quantum field, and argue that this same peculiarity makes it a gateway to cosmology and other sectors. I then turn to a less technical question: how should a field plan for exploration when no theorem guarantees the next discovery? My answer is to pursue precision without pretending to know in advance which measurement will matter, sustain a diverse experimental portfolio, protect theoretical risk-taking, and make the public case for fundamental exploration on its own terms.

titles.title: After the Higgs: Looking for the Universe Behind the Particle

abstracts.value: In conditioned generative models of physical systems, the densities at different values of the conditioning parameters are often related through symplectic transformations. For stable linear Hamiltonian systems, there exists a symplectic transformation to "normal coordinates" such that the dynamics is reduced to rotations in each phase-space plane. This picture extends to the nonlinear case where, away from resonances, the Birkhoff normal form again consists of rotations in phase space, now with amplitude dependence. In this work, we introduce an invertible symplectic flow layer consisting of amplitude-dependent rotations in learned normal coordinates. We derive the condition under which the nonlinear rotation layer is symplectic and detail an architecture that guarantees it. Experiments are carried out on three conditional generative modeling problems: a synthetic chain of coupled nonlinear oscillators and two problems from accelerator physics. We show empirically that normalizing flows with the new layers achieve competitive or superior negative log-likelihoods compared to baseline flows, with gains that grow with the strength of the nonlinearity on the synthetic system.

titles.title: Symplectic Normal Coordinates Flow for Generative Modeling of Hamiltonian Systems

abstracts.value: Generative samplers for lattice field theory are commonly evaluated by their effective sample size (ESS). We show that a small global ESS need not imply inaccurate long-distance observables: errors spread over many short-distance modes can dominate this diagnostic. We introduce a scale-resolved diagnostic based on the overlap between coarse-grained model and target distributions. At the lattice cutoff, this overlap determines the asymptotic ESS fraction; lower cutoffs isolate long-wavelength errors. In the exactly solvable free theory, two samplers with comparable ESS yield a $32\%$ bias and no bias in the susceptibility, respectively. In two-dimensional $ϕ^4$ theory near criticality, trained diffusion samplers show the same separation of scales: their path-weight ESS fraction falls rapidly over the volumes studied, while low moments of the magnetization remain close to their target values. Varying the reference parameters substantially changes infrared observables, with little effect on the log-weight variance. Given the target magnetization distribution, a marginal Metropolis test maintains an acceptance rate of order one in our tests. Combined with exact local updates, it reduces the remaining mismatch, although residual bias remains at finite relaxation length. In the free field, uniformly bounded relative errors in the proposal mode variances give a volume-independent bound on the number of updates needed for a prescribed accuracy of the chain's stationary mode variances at fixed correlation length. The target marginal must be supplied or computed separately; estimating it from the samplers' own weights can inherit the poor global overlap.

titles.title: Evaluating generative samplers for lattice field theory by scale

abstracts.value: Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) optimize circuit angles through repeated quantum-device evaluations, often facing vanishing gradients and high optimization costs. We ask whether a large language model (LLM) can write these angles directly. Extending *weight-space programming* from classical networks to quantum circuits, we provide a frontier LLM (\gpt) with the problem, circuit, and gate conventions. Its angles are executed exactly as written, without returning losses, gradients, or accuracy feedback. Across 139 requests, we test handwritten-digit classification, VQE ground-state estimation for spin chains and H$_2$, and MaxCut QAOA, comparing against random weights, classical optimization, and optimization initialized with LLM weights on the same circuit. When parameters have interpretable structure, the LLM matches or approaches the optimizer: it achieves 95--100% of the energy spectrum on every VQE problem, derives the exact H$_2$ ground state in closed form, finds optimal depth-one QAOA angles for every graph, and reaches 93--96% accuracy on digits 3 versus 8 with 12--18 hand-written weights, outperforming an optimizer trained on the same ten examples. Its weights are also strong warm starts: optimization reaches its best value after a median of one evaluation rather than hundreds. Allowed to design circuits, the LLM chooses data-dependent rotation chains encoding pixel importance in all 30 cases (one qubit for binary tasks, one chain per qubit for ten classes), reaching 65% accuracy across ten digits. Yet the approach fails in opaque weight spaces: accuracy drops to chance when fixed circuits exceed 30 weights, while optimization improves. It is also sensitive to gate conventions: 6 of 42 QAOA replies reverse mixing-angle signs and fail. We release all prompts, replies, and scores.

titles.title: Weight-Space Programming of Variational Quantum Circuits: Large Language Models Write Quantum Circuit Parameters Without an Optimizer

abstracts.value: We give an exposition of a recent proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis conjecture, which states that every degree-$d$ polynomial $p : \{0,1\}^n \to [0,1]$ has a variable of influence at least $\mathrm{poly}(\mathrm{Var}(p)/d)$. This implies that quantum query algorithms for decision problems can be efficiently simulated classically on most inputs. It also yields a near-equivalence between the status of the $\mathsf{BPP}$ vs. $\mathsf{BQP}$ problem in the random oracle and unrelativized worlds. We organize the proof around four main steps and discuss how each connects to the literature on the analysis of boolean functions and probabilistic combinatorics. To bring out the key ideas, we do not optimize parameters, and our presentation yields weaker exponents than the original. $\textbf{Authors' note.}$ The proof was discovered by David Turturean using a research system developed at Physical Superintelligence (PSI), in combination with a non-public Anthropic model. The proof was then shared with the authors, who worked to understand it and prepare this exposition. Anthropic's public models were used in this process. The authors did not receive financial compensation from Anthropic or PSI. This article is not intended for publication at a conference or in a journal.

titles.title: Proof of the Aaronson-Ambainis Conjecture: An Exposition

abstracts.value: We present PC-QEC, a proof-carrying compilation framework for quantum error correction parameterized by both code distance and syndrome-extraction scheme. It covers all four schemes---Standard, Flag, Shor and Knill---with circuit-level distance guarantees for every legal code distance in each proved family under the declared fault and readout contracts. The circuit-level model permits single-wire Pauli faults at every operation's qubit operands, capturing data errors, readout errors and ancilla faults that propagate into multi-qubit hook errors. For each family and scheme, code-algebra proofs and fault-aware Hoare proofs compose into a finite symbolic certificate whose size is independent of code distance. We demonstrate family-wide guarantees for five code families across all four schemes. For rotated Surface code, one Standard Scheme certificate proves a distance lower bound $d$ for every odd $d\ge3$ and checks in 214 s on average. Lean 4 mechanizes the metatheory and exact circuit-level distances for canonical Surface, hypergraph-product (HGP) and Toric code families.

titles.title: Parametric Proof-Carrying Compilation for Quantum Error-Correction

abstracts.value: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.

titles.title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits

abstracts.value: The $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)^{168}\mathrm{Tm}$ cross section has been measured at the Shanghai Laser Electron Gamma Source (SLEGS) using quasi-monoenergetic laser-Compton-scattering $γ$ rays over the energy range from the neutron threshold to 14.61~MeV. The photon flux and energy distribution were determined with a LaBr$3$(Ce) spectrometer, and monoenergetic cross sections were obtained using an iterative unfolding method. Below 12~MeV, the present cross sections agree well with the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluations. However, near the maximum of the $(γ,n)$ excitation function, the present cross sections are significantly higher than both the NewSUBARU data and the IAEA-2019 evaluated values. The $E1$$γ$-ray strength functions were derived by fitting the experimental cross sections measured at SLEGS and NewSUBARU. The stellar reaction rates for $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)$ and $^{168}\mathrm{Tm}(n,γ)$ were calculated by incorporating these constrained $γ$-ray strength functions into the TALYS code. The calculated $^{169}\mathrm{Tm}(γ,n)$ rates were adopted in a full $p$-process reaction network for the shock-heated O/Ne-rich layers of a $20 M\odot$ core-collapse supernova model to perform a sensitivity analysis. The updated rates have a negligible effect on the final $p$-nucleus abundances.

titles.title: Measurement of the $^{169}$Tm$(γ,n)$$^{168}$Tm Cross Section and Implications for $γ$-Process Calculations

abstracts.value: We investigate the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ gravity model, $f(Q,T) = αQ^n + βT + γ$, which represents a nontrivial coupling between geometry and matter in the context of a dust-dominated Universe. The model parameters $(H_0, α, β, γ, n)$ are constrained using recent cosmological observations, including Hubble parameter measurements $H(z)$, the Pantheon+SH0ES dataset, and DESI BAO data. The analysis shows that the Hubble constant exhibits dataset-dependent variations, reflecting the persisting Hubble tension, while $α$ and $γ$ are tightly constrained and $β$ remains weakly determined. The nonlinear exponent $n$ introduces an additional degree of freedom that enhances the model's flexibility in reproducing observational trends. The cosmographic diagnostics, including the deceleration, jerk, snap, and lerk parameters, indicate a Universe transitioning from early deceleration to late-time acceleration, with present values closely aligned with $Λ$CDM predictions and far-future behavior approaching a de Sitter phase. These results demonstrate that the nonlinear $f(Q,T)$ model provides a simple and viable framework to describe late-time cosmic acceleration, accommodate observational tensions, and reproduce $Λ$CDM-like dynamics with subtle deviations.

titles.title: Dust matter cosmology in modified symmetric teleparallel $f(Q,T)$ gravity

abstracts.value: We investigate the collective dynamics of a bundle of charged particles undergoing cyclotron motion in a uniform magnetic field when subjected to a short-duration electric pulse. Using the geometric framework based on the evolution of trajectory congruences, we analyze how the pulse affects the expansion, shear, and rotation of a small family of trajectories. We show that the geometric imprint persists after the pulse has vanished, manifesting as a memory of the transient perturbation. Unlike gravitational memory effects, this does not manifest itself in focusing behavior of the trajectories, and instead implies a restructuring of the shear component before and after the pulse. We offer direct analytic and regression-based arguments for the same.

abstracts.value: The Segmented Inverted-coaxial GerMAnium (SIGMA) detector is a large-volume, position-sensitive high-purity germanium detector developed for <math altimg="si80.svg" display="inline" id="d1e837"><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray tracking and imaging. The SIGMA detector features an inverted-coaxial geometry with a unique configuration of 18 segments providing position sensitivity, complemented by small point-contact technology for excellent energy resolution. In this work, the position resolution of SIGMA has been experimentally evaluated using pulse shape analysis with a simulated signal database generated using the AGATA Detector Library. The simulated response was validated against experimental signals and optimised through variation of the detector impurity concentration and charge-carrier mobility parameters. At 662 keV, the radial position resolution was found to be 2.8 mm in the outer-segment region and 4.1 mm in the core region, with an azimuthal resolution of approximately 7° and a position resolution through depth along the crystal length of 2.4 mm. After correcting for the contributions from the finite <math altimg="si80.svg" display="inline" id="d1e842"><mi>γ</mi></math>-ray beam width and the granularity of the database, the intrinsic resolution was found to be 2.5 mm (outer) and 3.9 mm (core) radially, 6.5° azimuthally, and 2.0 mm through depth. The resulting intrinsic three-dimensional resolution was determined to be 3.8 mm in the outer-segment region and 4.5 mm in the core region, consistent with previous simulation predictions for standalone operation of the detector. These results represent the first experimental position resolution measurements for the SIGMA detector.

titles.title: Experimental position resolution of the segmented inverted-coaxial germanium detector, SIGMA

abstracts.value: Fault-tolerant quantum computing reached a milestone in December 2024 when Google's Willow processor demonstrated below-threshold error correction on a superconducting chip, a result since reproduced on neutral-atom and alternative superconducting platforms. Yet the classical decoders needed to sustain this performance face a scaling challenge: noise becomes increasingly structured and correlated as systems grow, while decoders must respond within microsecond coherence windows. This survey asks whether error suppression, noise diagnosis, and decoding are better treated as one adaptive control problem than as three separate research programs. Drawing on a scoping review of 146 records, it organizes the field into a three-layer taxonomy. Layer 1 (Hardware-Level Suppression) integrates protection into the physical substrate; bosonic cat qubits exponentially suppress bit-flip errors, projecting up to 90% overhead reduction versus surface codes. Layer 2 (Diagnosis) employs probabilistic models and computational intelligence to characterize error sources; neuro-fuzzy architectures and the Bias-Entropy decomposition separate hardware drift from logical faults, subject to an identifiability limit that we characterize. Layer 3 (Real-time Decoding) targets the integration of machine learning within strict latency constraints. Hardware acceleration now approaches superconducting cycle times, which shifts the case for learned decoders from speed toward accuracy under correlated noise; recent advances favor hybrid, physics-informed architectures: Neural Belief Propagation resolves degeneracy issues in quantum low-density parity-check codes by embedding topological constraints directly into the network's loss function. These results suggest a transition toward closed-loop AI architectures that treat error management as continuous control rather than static algorithm selection.

titles.title: Adaptive error management for fault-tolerant quantum computing across hardware-level suppression, system-level diagnosis, and real-time decoding

abstracts.value: We analyze the spectrum of quantum square lattice graph exposed to a homogeneous magnetic field with a rational flux through plaquette, assuming all nontrivial cases of the vertex coupling which is circulant and scale-invariant, with a particular attention to those of them that give rise to a dynamics violating the time reversal invariance. Except for two cases with partially decoupled edges, the remaining twelve split into two spectral classes; the second one offers a hitherto unknown butterfly pattern.

titles.title: A new butterfly in the meadow: magnetic lattice graphs with a circulant vertex coupling

abstracts.value: The deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$ of type $D_l$ possesses an infinite family of commuting elements that can be viewed as a two-parameter deformation of the classical Hamiltonians for the KdV hierarchy of type $D_l$; these conserved charges are termed local integrals of motion (IMs). Concurrently, the quantum toroidal algebra $U_q(D_l^{"})$ of type $D_l$ admits four distinct representations via free field realizations, each corresponding to one of the four end nodes of the affine Dynkin diagram. Utilizing these representations, we associate an infinite set of commuting operators with each node, which we define as non-local integrals of motion. Both local and non-local integrals of motion act simultaneously on a shared Fock space consisting of $l+1$ free fields. We provide a direct, computational proof demonstrating that these local and non-local integrals of motion mutually commute.

titles.title: Integrals of motion for the deformed $W$-algebra $W_{q,t}(D_l)$

abstracts.value: Variational quantum classifiers can generate highly structured decision boundaries through the Fourier dependence of observable expectation values on circuit parameters. We show that expressivity can come at a sharp statistical cost, by considering a quantum perceptron whose readout is the simplest periodic classifier, namely a square-wave function of the weighted inputs, and determine its typical generalization in the thermodynamic limit using a teacher-student replica-symmetric theory. Above a critical oscillation frequency, increasing the training load induces a first-order transition from weakly to strongly teacher-aligned phases, resulting in a discontinuous improvement in generalization. At fixed load, however, increasing the frequency eventually drives the equilibrium generalization error to chance level, despite perfect classification of all the training examples. Thus, the same periodic structure that enhances random-label storage can delay the onset of learning. Our results expose a quantitative tradeoff between memorization and generalization generated purely by periodic readout, and provide a benchmark for understanding Fourier-rich variational quantum classifiers.

titles.title: Periodic Readout Induces a First-Order Generalization Transition in a Quantum Perceptron

abstracts.value: Given a finite nonlocal game, can the players win with certainty? We prove that the existence of a perfect normal spatial strategy is $Σ^0_2$-complete, even when restricted to games of value one, so it cannot be decided even with an oracle for the halting problem. This is strictly harder than perfect play in the finite-dimensional and commuting-operator models, which are $Σ^0_1$-complete and $Π^0_1$-complete. Within the commuting model, the existence of a perfect normal strategy with a finite or semifinite von Neumann host is $Σ^0_2$-complete, whereas for every fixed type $\mathrm{III}_λ$ subtype it has the same $Π^0_1$-complete language as unrestricted commuting play. A trace thus costs one existential number quantifier: the hardness constructions force every perfect strategy to choose a finite clock period or a finite tree depth. Spatial $Σ^0_2$-completeness also holds when finite entanglement entropy is required, and both forms are formally verified in Lean. For every computable $0<α<1$, perfect spatial play with $\mathrm{Tr}\,h^α<\infty$ for the reduced density $h$ is $Σ^0_2$-complete as well; these conditions form a strict ladder between finite rank and finite entropy. We also prove $Σ^0_2$-completeness for one-shot zero-error communication with normal entanglement, and construct a finite channel with zero-error codes of a given size each of which needs infinite entanglement entropy.

titles.title: A trace costs one quantifier: the exact complexity of perfect play in nonlocal games

abstracts.value: For a random matrix, with eigenvalues in a one-body potential $V(x)$ and a 2-body interaction $R(x,x')$, it is known that the resolvent converges in the large $N$ limit to an analytic function in the complex plane minus cuts, called the spectral curve. In the 1-cut case, a two-sheeted neighborhood of the cut is a cylinder with two simple ramification points. We describe these spectral curve data by boundary integral operators and generalized cycles. Vice-versa, given a 2-branchpoints spectral curve in a cylinder, there exists a formal random matrix model that corresponds to it. The goal of this article is to show the method to recover a formal random matrix model, with its potential and 2-body interaction, from the geometry of the spectral curve.

titles.title: Cylinder spectral curve and 1-cut Matrix model

abstracts.value: We study positivity and rigidity for an expanding quasi-local energy $E_λ$ associated with constantly umbilic initial data $(Ω,g,k=λg)$, introduced in earlier work [ALP26] as an analogue of the Brown-York energy adapted to an expanding flat de Sitter background. Under nonnegative scalar curvature and suitable boundary assumptions, our previous results established positivity for $λ$ below a geometrically determined threshold $α$, while vanishing $E_λ$ at $λ=α$ forced the boundary to be round. In this paper, we strengthen this endpoint rigidity statement by showing that, if $E_λ=0$ when $λ=α$, then $(Ω,g)$ is isometric to a closed Euclidean 3-ball of radius at most $1/λ$. The proof combines the rigidity theorem of Shi-Tam for the Brown-York energy with a strict concavity argument. We also construct an explicit counterexample to the positivity and rigidity conjecture formulated in [ALP26], showing that the energy can become negative beyond this threshold and that vanishing energy need not imply rigidity.

titles.title: A note on Positivity and Rigidity for an Expanding Quasi-Local Energy

abstracts.value: Most proposed applications of boson samplers, including photonic machine-learning models, do not use the samples themselves but estimates of output probabilities, marginals or overlaps, obtained to additive precision from a finite number of shots. For product inputs such as single photons, these quantities can already be estimated classically with Gurvits's algorithm and its generalisations. We ask whether entangled inputs change this picture. For any $n$-photon input that is a matrix-product state of bond dimension $χ$, with one photon per site and $L$ modes per site, we give an unbiased estimator of any output amplitude of an $m$-mode interferometer, whose mean-square error after $N$ draws is at most $\|ψ\|^2/N$ whatever the interferometer, the output pattern and the entanglement of the state. Each draw costs $O(nLχ^2+nL^3+mn)$ operations after $O(nLχ^3)$ preprocessing, and an additive error $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $1-δ$ requires $O(\|ψ\|^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/δ))$ draws, with memory of the order of the input size. The main application is to light emitted sequentially by quantum emitters, such as spin-based sources of photonic cluster states, for which $χ$ is bounded by the dimension of the source's retained quantum memory: one spin gives $χ=2$ at any length, and a memory of $k$ qubits, held in emitters or in photons stored in a delay line, gives $χ\le2^k$, so the cost stays polynomial as long as $k=O(\log n)$. The same sampler also estimates traced-memory probabilities, overlaps and individual marginal probabilities. All guarantees are additive: the estimator gives neither relative estimates of exponentially small probabilities nor a sampler of the output distribution.

titles.title: On the estimation of linear-optical amplitudes and probabilities with entangled input state

abstracts.value: The dissipative properties of isoscalar collective motion in heavy nuclei are studied within a kinetic model of collective excitations in finite Fermi systems with a free moving surface. The model includes both the one-body damping produced by the interaction of nucleons with the dynamic surface of nucleus and the Landau damping mechanism. In this paper, we study the damping and dissipative properties of the isoscalar dipole collective modes and the isoscalar vortex octupole mode, which are formed due to dynamic effects of the nuclear surface. To study the damping mechanism of the considered collective modes, a multipole strength function is used in various approximations. It is shown that the damping of the considered isoscalar collective modes is due to a one-body damping mechanism. An analytical expression for the dissipation coefficient at finite frequency for the collective variable describing multipole oscillations of nuclear surface is obtained. It was found that the dissipation coefficient in the energy region of the considered isoscalar collective modes does not exceed the wall formula friction coefficient derived in the one-body dissipation theory. This result confirms the understanding of friction in the wall formula as a macroscopic limit of the one-body nuclear dissipation.

titles.title: Dissipative properties of isoscalar collective excitations in heavy nuclei

abstracts.value: Simulating high dimensional unstructured Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with quantum processors is a major challenge with significant potential benefit. Existing methods have been demonstrated at small qubit counts, on simplifications of realistic problems. We implement a quantum reservoir network (QRN) for forecasting high-dimensional unstructured PDEs using up to 52 qubits on IBM superconducting hardware. Our method is gradient-free and does not suffer from the challenges of variational quantum algorithms. Instead, the QRN provides a large kernel space, up to 2^52 dimensions and beyond the reach of exact classical simulation, that remains useful under current hardware noise levels. Furthermore, a partial measure-and-reset mechanism enables total circuit runtime for ~24 times the qubit coherence time, so qubit lifetimes do not limit the forecast horizon. Thus, our method enables forecasting realistic unstructured nonlinear PDEs on quantum hardware. Typical difficulties associated with predicting large scale PDEs, such as transpilation, exponential shot requirements, hardware noise, and short qubit lifetimes are mitigated through careful design considerations and a dynamic observable reconstruction method. We validate our approach using a ~34k cell unstructured 2D cylinder flow at Reynolds number 1000 and a challenging nonlinear Gray--Scott reaction--diffusion problem, demonstrating high fidelity prediction on CUDA-Q simulation and on 26 and 52-qubit superconducting quantum processors. Specifically, we show that adding QRN features to an autoencoder linear prediction pipeline reduces prediction error by 21%-43%. Finally, we demonstrate closed-loop autoregressive PDE forecasting on these problems. This work demonstrates, for the first time, quantum circuits with depth beyond qubit lifetimes achieving accurate unstructured mesh forecasting on highly nonlinear PDEs.

titles.title: Realizing Unstructured PDE Forecasting on Superconducting Quantum Processors

abstracts.value: We present a global analysis of the semileptonic transitions $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ and $B_c\to(η_c,B,B_s)$ by comparing five potential-model implementations of the QCD-motivated light-front quark model. We use the same fully Bakamjian--Thomas-based prescription for the weak current in all five models and keep their respective spectroscopic parameters fixed. We examine how confinement, radial mixing, and the treatment of hyperfine interactions jointly affect the form factors, differential decay rates, branching fractions, and lepton-flavor ratios. The internal Lorentz prefactors use the same free quark--antiquark kinematics as the on-shell constituent spinors in the weak-current kernels, while the physical meson masses determine the external kinematics. For each model and decay channel, the two independent extractions of $f_-(q^2)$ using the $(+,\perp)$ and $(+,-)$ current-component combinations agree within numerical accuracy. We perform a direct analytic continuation of the spacelike overlap integrals in the $q^+=0$ frame using a mass-weighted contour in complex transverse momentum space. This yields the form factors throughout the physical timelike region, including zero recoil, without parametrizing their $q^2$ dependence. Form factors and differential decay rates are presented as equal-weight model averages with pointwise minimum--maximum bands. The light-lepton-averaged ratios range from $0.282$ to $0.301$ for $R(D)$ and from $0.287$ to $0.303$ for $R(D_s)$.

titles.title: A comparative analysis of semileptonic $B_{(s)}\to D_{(s)}$ and $B_c\to(η_c,B,B_s)$ decays in the light-front quark model

abstracts.value: We report the detection of $\sim$280-day quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) in the SMMAN observations of PKS 0754+100 at 4.8 and 23.6 GHz, which may also be present in VLBI observations made at 15 GHz. The onset of a transition of the amplitude of variability in the radio flux density, observed more clearly in the 15 GHz and 23.6 GHz observations, coincides with the detection of a likely QPO of $\sim$1.4 days in optical observations made by the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite. This transition in radio variability also occurs close in time to the disappearance of the secondary knot in the VLBI radio map during the lower variability state. An X-ray flare was observed 100 days before this transition, suggesting that the mechanisms causing these quasi-periodicities are related. After the transition to a higher variability state, both the 15 and 23.6 GHz light curves exhibit indications of QPOs at $\sim$400 days. For the first time, a QPO detected in the radio band from a BL Lac has been seen to appear to shift to a QPO of lower frequency, with that transition occurring near the appearance of a QPO in optical emission at a much shorter period. This multi-waveband behavior could be related to the internal helical structure of the jet, where an instability or kink develops due to magnetic reconnection and propagates outward.

titles.title: SMMAN studies of AGN variability. II. Radio and optical quasi-periodic oscillations and changing variability states in the relativistic jet of the blazar PKS 0754+100

abstracts.value: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) remains a cornerstone hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for quantum simulation, yet its scalability is fundamentally constrained by heavy measurement overheads. While strategies such as variance-preserved shot reduction (VPSR) mitigates this cost, they suffer from convergence instability and optimization stagnation caused by finite-sample bias in limited pilot shots. To overcome this limitation, we introduce delta-corrected shot reduction (DCSR), an analytically enhanced shot allocation strategy that rigorously mitigates finite-sample instability. Utilizing the multivariate delta method, we derive explicit higher-order bias correction terms for the empirical reduction factor. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations reveal that incorporating higher-order statistical moments, such as skewness and kurtosis, provides the gradient resolution necessary to bypass noise-induced barren plateaus. DSCR significantly accelerates convergence compared to standard VPSR across diverse noise and resource regimes while matching or decreasing cumulative measurement costs, establishing a mathematically rigorous framework for variance-stabilized shot allocation on near-term hardware.

titles.title: Delta-Corrected Shot Reduction for Bypassing Optimization Plateaus in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers

abstracts.value: The fission of $^{180}\mathrm{Hg}$ is investigated by studying the stochastic evolution on the potential energy surface calculated within the multidimensionally constrained relativistic Hartree--Bogoliubov (MDC-RHB) model. The MDC-RHB model provides the zero-temperature potential-energy surface in the $(β_{20},β_{30})$ plane and self-consistent density distributions, from which scission configurations are identified using a geometrical neck criterion. The evolution toward scission is described by a master equation on the same deformation mesh, with transition rates determined by deformation-dependent microscopic level densities. The level densities are obtained in a finite-temperature BCS treatment using the MDC-RHB single-particle spectra and zero-temperature pairing gaps as input. The effective barrier-top region is found to lie close to the scission line, making the detailed energetic structure of the scission boundary particularly important for the fragment distribution. The potential-energy landscape and scission-line structure strongly favor reflection-asymmetric configurations with pronounced prefragment deformations and lead to fragment-mass distributions centered close to the experimentally observed $A_{\mathrm L}/A_{\mathrm H}\simeq80/100$ division. An additional constrained $β_{40}$ analysis indicates that fluctuations beyond the $(β_{20},β_{30})$ collective space can generate an additional spread of the fragment masses. With increasing excitation energy over the range $E^*=34.0$--$65.5$ MeV, the symmetric component is enhanced, while the asymmetric fission mode remains dominant.

titles.title: Role of the scission-line structure in the formation of the fragment-mass distribution in $^{180}$Hg fission

abstracts.value: Thouless pumping provides a powerful route for probing Chern topology through quantized motion in one-dimensional lattices. We investigate such a topological pump in an extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with tunable next-nearest-neighbor hoppings. A graphical representation in Bloch space is used to construct pumping schemes. In this framework, the Bloch vector traces a closed loop that evolves in time. The Chern number of the synthetic band is then determined by the motion of this loop. Quantum pumping phenomena are demonstrated for a filled band and for a bosonic wave packet driven by Bloch oscillations. We further show that the Haldane model can be mapped to the driven extended SSH chain by replacing a quasimomentum by the pumping time. The quantized charge pump indicates that the Chern number of a two-dimensional model can be read out from a one-dimensional pumping protocol, offering an accessible route for detecting higher-dimensional topology, such as in photonic and cold-atom platforms.

titles.title: Thouless pumping and Haldane-model topology in a driven extended SSH chain

abstracts.value: Pure states of quantum many-body systems at thermal equilibrium are known to be typical, in a sense that a randomly chosen pure state from an appropriate energy shell reproduces the Gibbs-state expectation values of most observables acting on a small subsystem. However, such typical states are intrinsically stochastic, conventionally generated from the random high-temperature state, suffer from statistical fluctuations, and do not provide a continuous connection to the ground state. Here, we introduce a deterministic variational framework for constructing a Markov-Shielded Typical (MST) state, a unique thermal pure-state representative whose local reduced density matrices closely approximate those of the Gibbs state, from the ground state up to infinite-temperature limit. Our approach reformulates free-energy minimization by replacing the nonlocal von Neumann entropy with a local, computationally tractable Markov entropy, where we establish rigorous upper and lower bounds of MST free energy to lie in the very vicinity of the thermal free energy. This framework extends the concept of typicality to deterministic pure-state representations of thermal equilibrium, offering a scalable wave-function approach with potential applications to both classical and quantum computing.

titles.title: Markov-Shielded Typicality for Thermal Quantum States

abstracts.value: In conventional quantum mechanics, the Hamiltonian is required to be Hermitian, ensuring real energy eigenvalues. Certain non-Hermitian Hamiltonians can also possess entirely real spectra when they are invariant under the combined action of parity ($\mathcal P$) and time reversal ($\mathcal T$). Such Hamiltonians are called unbroken parity--time ($\mathcal{PT}$)-symmetric. We conjecture that, in a string-inspired scenario, a repulsive phase of gravity may be due to a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric gravitational theory, characterised by anomalous Chern-Simons terms, coupled to axion fields. The conjecture is based on the behaviour of the chiral anomalous couplings of these axions to electromagnetic potentials. Within the Exact Renormalisation Group (ERG) framework in the modified local potential approximation, we argue that singularities in the ERG beta functions for such couplings may indicate an infrared phase transition. At the energy scales of these singularities, we conjecture that the field theory transitions from the Hermitian phase to a ${\mathcal P}{\mathcal T}$-- symmetric theory, of gravity, characterised by a repulsive Netwon's ``constant''. This may induce the acceleration observed in the Universe at late eras, without the need for a dark--energy component.

titles.title: ERG, axions, and a PT-symmetric accelerating Universe

abstracts.value: We investigate the evolution of an axisymmetric black hole magnetosphere using general relativistic particle-in-cell simulations, focusing on its global current structure, variability, and radiative effects. We include inverse-Compton (IC) scattering of ambient photons and subsequent two-photon pair production, and compare simulations with and without synchrotron-curvature (SC) radiation reaction. Starting from an axisymmetric vertical magnetic field, the system develops a polar spark gap and a variable equatorial current sheet that together sustain the global poloidal current. For the parameters explored in this study, we observe that the spark gap oscillates upon the onset of SC cooling, whereas the current sheet is less sensitive to radiative cooling. Time-dependent electric fields in the return-current layer trigger magnetic-field rearrangement followed by magnetic reconnection. Cross-correlation analysis finds no significant correlation between the two regions' variability, suggesting dynamical independence. We further perform post-processing ray-tracing calculations to evaluate the radiative efficiencies of the IC and SC processes. High-energy particles dominate the bolometric luminosity, which reaches up to 1 percent of the Blandford-Znajek luminosity for SC emission and 0.1 percent for IC emission. The relative IC luminosity to SC is higher at lower viewing angles because particle momenta are more anisotropic near the pole than near the equator, due to efficient acceleration along the local magnetic field lines. Together with energetic estimates, these results suggest that both regions can contribute to high-energy emission in active galactic nuclei, with spark-gap photons reaching the sub-TeV regime.

abstracts.value: This paper investigates non-relativistic supersymmetric gauge theories obtained through null reduction, with particular focus on supersymmetric Abelian Higgs models and their soliton solutions. Starting from four-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 1$ relativistic supersymmetric theories, we apply null reduction to derive Galilean-invariant non-relativistic theories in $2 + 1$ dimensions while preserving gauge symmetry and supersymmetry. The resulting symmetry structure is shown to correspond to the Bargmann extension of the super-Galilean algebra. We first analyze the massive supersymmetric Abelian Higgs model and show that, although it possesses nontrivial vacuum configurations, the mass term obstructs the existence of nontrivial BPS vortex solutions. We then study the massless supersymmetric Abelian Higgs model with multiple charged scalar fields, for which the BPS equations admit vortex-type soliton solutions under suitable charge and winding number conditions. The vacuum moduli space is identified as a weighted projective space, leading naturally to both integer and fractional vortex configurations. By imposing radial symmetry, we derive the corresponding vortex equations and examine their solutions analytically and numerically. Finally, we relate the vacuum structure of the model to the Ginzburg-Landau theory of superconductivity, highlighting how familiar superconducting behavior can emerge from a symmetry-preserving non-relativistic supersymmetric framework.

titles.title: Non-Relativistic Supersymmetric Gauge Theories and Soliton Solutions

abstracts.value: We demonstrate a novel QKD protocol, named \texttt{Bridge[$d,q$]}, which generalizes the \texttt{SARG04} protocol to $d$ dimensions and $q$ bases. In this protocol, Alice and Bob gain only partial knowledge about each other's raw key. Nevertheless, this partial information is sufficient to distill a definite mutual encryption key. We present an experimental demonstration of the \texttt{Bridge[$2,3$]} protocol. The three unbiased polarization bases were switched using a single Pockels cell. The applied polarization basis switching method is relevant to any 3-basis QKD protocol and to other applications that require fast manipulation of photon polarization qubits.

titles.title: Demonstration of a partial knowledge quantum key distribution protocol
